It encompasses various aspects of games, including their design, mechanics, aesthetics, social and cultural impact, and player experiences.

sublevels.name: Sound Studies
sublevels.description: Sound Studies is an interdisciplinary field exploring the cultural, historical, and technological dimensions of sound and listening. It examines how practices like voice, noise, silence, and aural perception are shaped by society and media, with an emphasis on sound reproduction technologies.

sublevels.name: International and Intercultural Communication
sublevels.description: Intercultural communication refers to how communication behavior is affected when people from different cultures interact and differ in how they perceive the world around them. One way to understand intercultural communication is to see it as communication that unfolds in symbolic intercultural spaces.

sublevels.name: Media and Gender
sublevels.description: Media and gender refers to the relationship between mass media and gender, and how gender is represented within media platforms.

sublevels.name: Media and Globalisation
sublevels.description: The process of the production, distribution, and consumption of media products on a global scale, facilitating the exchange and diffusion of ideas cross-culturally.

sublevels.name: Business and Management
sublevels.description: Management (or managing) is the administration of an organization, whether it is a business, a nonprofit organization, or a government body. It is the art and science of managing the resources of the business. Management includes the activities of setting the strategy of an organization and coordinating the efforts of its employees (or of volunteers) to accomplish its objectives through the application of available resources, such as financial, natural, technological, and human resources.

sublevels.name: Industries
sublevels.description: Industry studies in the field of business and management refer to the examination and analysis of specific industries, such as healthcare, finance, or retail. It involves studying the economic, social, and technological trends, as well as the regulatory environment and competitive landscape of an industry to understand its performance and growth potential. Industry studies can be conducted by both academic researchers and practitioners, including business analysts, consultants, and policymakers. The aim of industry studies is to provide insights into how businesses can operate more efficiently and effectively within a given industry, as well as to inform policy decisions that may affect the industry as a whole. The topics within industry studies may include market structure, supply chains, innovation, pricing strategies, consumer behavior, and corporate social responsibility, among others.

sublevels.name: Trade and Retail
sublevels.description: The Trade and Retail industry, also known as the Retail sector, is a field within business and management research and practice that focuses on the process of selling consumer goods or services to customers through physical stores or online platforms. The core topics in this field include: Consumer behavior: studying the behavior of consumers in terms of their needs, preferences, and shopping patterns. Marketing and advertising: developing and implementing strategies to promote products and services to target customers, through advertising, branding, and other marketing techniques. Sales management: managing and coordinating sales teams and developing effective sales strategies to drive revenue growth. Supply chain management: managing the flow of goods and services from suppliers to customers, including logistics, inventory management, and distribution. Retail operations: managing the day-to-day operations of retail stores, including staffing, store layout, and inventory management. E-commerce: understanding the online retail environment and developing strategies for online sales, including website design, social media marketing, and search engine optimization. Customer service: developing strategies to provide high-quality customer service, including training staff, developing policies, and measuring customer satisfaction. Store design and visual merchandising: designing store layouts and displays to attract customers and maximize sales. Retail analytics: analyzing data on consumer behavior, sales, and other metrics to inform business decisions and improve performance. Retail innovation: exploring new technologies and trends in the industry, including the use of artificial intelligence, virtual reality, and other digital tools to enhance the retail experience.

sublevels.name: Business Consulting
sublevels.description: The consulting industry is a field of business and management research that focuses on the study of consulting firms, their operations, and their impact on clients and industries. This research area includes various topics such as the role of consulting firms in strategy development, the impact of consulting services on organizational performance, the management of consulting projects, the effectiveness of consulting interventions, and the evolution of the consulting industry over time. Studies in this field also analyze the structure of consulting firms, the skills and competencies required for consulting, and the dynamics of client-consultant relationships. Overall, the consulting industry is an important area of research for understanding the strategic and operational challenges faced by organizations in various industries and the role of consulting firms in addressing them.

sublevels.name: Real Estate Management
sublevels.description: Real Estate and Facilities Management is a field within business and management that focuses on the management, operation, and maintenance of real estate properties and facilities. The field includes various topics such as: Real estate investment and analysis,, Property valuation and appraisal, Property and facilities management, Lease negotiation and management, Property and facilities maintenance, Sustainability in real estate and facilities management, Workplace design and management, Risk management in real estate and facilities management, Technology and innovation in real estate and facilities management, Asset management and performance measurement.

sublevels.name: Luxury
sublevels.description: The luxury industry is a field of business and management research that focuses on the production, marketing, and consumption of luxury goods and services. It involves a wide range of industries, including fashion, beauty, jewelry, watches, automobiles, hospitality, and more. Core topics within the luxury industry field of research may include consumer behavior and preferences, brand management, product design and development, pricing strategies, distribution and retail management, supply chain management, digital marketing and e-commerce, sustainability and social responsibility, and global luxury markets and trends. Additionally, research in this field may explore the cultural, social, and psychological aspects of luxury consumption and how they influence consumer behavior and decision-making.

sublevels.name: Automotive Industry
sublevels.description: The automotive industry is a field of business and management research that focuses on the design, development, production, marketing, and sale of vehicles, including cars, trucks, buses, motorcycles, and other types of motorized vehicles. It encompasses a wide range of topics, such as supply chain management, manufacturing processes, technology and innovation, marketing strategies, consumer behavior, government regulations and policies, and sustainability. Researchers in this field may examine the performance and competitive strategies of individual companies, the dynamics of industry structure and competition, and the impact of technological advancements on the industry. The automotive industry has a significant economic impact worldwide and is of interest to scholars, policymakers, and practitioners alike.

sublevels.name: Services
sublevels.description: The services industry, also known as the service sector, encompasses a wide range of businesses that provide intangible products and services such as hospitality, banking, healthcare, education, insurance, and retail. It is a major contributor to many economies, accounting for a significant portion of the GDP in many countries.  As a field within business and management research and practice, the services industry involves studying and analyzing the unique challenges and opportunities faced by service-based businesses. Some core topics within this field include: Service quality and customer satisfaction: Ensuring that services meet or exceed customer expectations and result in high levels of satisfaction. Service innovation: Developing new and improved services to meet changing customer needs and preferences. Service marketing and branding: Promoting and positioning services effectively in the marketplace to attract and retain customers. Service operations management: Managing service delivery processes to ensure efficiency, quality, and customer satisfaction. Service design and delivery: Designing and delivering services that meet customer needs and preferences while optimizing resource utilization. Service personnel management: Managing the recruitment, training, and development of personnel in service organizations to ensure high levels of customer satisfaction. Service strategy and business models: Developing effective strategies and business models for service-based businesses in highly competitive and dynamic markets. Overall, research and practice in the services industry aim to improve the quality of service delivery, enhance customer satisfaction, and drive business growth and profitability in service-based businesses.

sublevels.name: Office Management
sublevels.description: Office Management is a field within business and management that involves the planning, organizing, and controlling of administrative activities, procedures, and resources to achieve organizational goals. It includes various administrative tasks such as managing office supplies, budgeting, coordinating meetings, managing employee schedules, and providing support to managers. Core topics within Office Management may include: Administrative support: This involves providing administrative support to managers and executives, including managing their schedules, preparing correspondence, and organizing meetings. Facilities management: This includes managing office spaces, ensuring proper maintenance of equipment, and overseeing office security.  Budgeting and financial management: This involves managing budgets, forecasting expenses, and analyzing financial reports. Human resource management: This includes managing employee records, coordinating recruitment and selection processes, and overseeing employee training and development. Project management: This involves managing projects from start to finish, including planning, budgeting, and executing tasks. Information management: This includes managing information systems, including data collection, storage, and analysis. Communication management: This involves managing communication within and outside the organization, including written and oral communication, social media management, and public relations. Overall, the core objective of Office Management is to ensure that all administrative tasks are handled efficiently and effectively, allowing the organization to operate smoothly and achieve its goals.

sublevels.name: Health Care Management
sublevels.description: Health Care Management is a field of business and management research that focuses on the organization, administration, and management of healthcare systems, facilities, and services. The core topics within this field include: Healthcare delivery systems: This includes the organization and management of healthcare delivery systems, including hospitals, clinics, long-term care facilities, and other healthcare organizations. Healthcare financing and economics: This includes the study of healthcare financing mechanisms, such as insurance, Medicaid and Medicare, and the economics of healthcare, such as cost-benefit analyses, cost-effectiveness studies, and healthcare spending. Healthcare policy and law: This includes the study of healthcare policy and regulations, such as HIPAA and the Affordable Care Act, as well as the legal and ethical issues related to healthcare, such as malpractice, patient privacy, and informed consent. Healthcare quality and patient safety: This includes the study of healthcare quality improvement, patient safety initiatives, and healthcare outcomes measurement. Healthcare information technology: This includes the study of healthcare information technology systems, such as electronic medical records, telemedicine, and health information exchanges. Healthcare workforce management: This includes the study of healthcare workforce planning and management, including recruitment, retention, training, and leadership development for healthcare professionals. Overall, Health Care Management seeks to improve the efficiency, effectiveness, and quality of healthcare services, while ensuring access to care for all patients.

sublevels.name: Non-Profit Organizations and Public Enterprises
sublevels.description: Non-profit organizations (NPOs) and public enterprises are an important area of research within the field of business and management. This area focuses on the management of organizations that operate in the public or non-profit sectors, such as government agencies, charities, foundations, and social enterprises. The core topics of research in this area include: Governance and leadership: This topic covers the management and governance of NPOs and public enterprises, including the role of the board, the CEO, and other leaders, as well as issues related to accountability and transparency. Strategy and planning: This topic covers the development and implementation of strategies and plans for NPOs and public enterprises, including issues related to stakeholder engagement, social impact, and sustainability. Fundraising and financial management: This topic covers the financial management and fundraising practices of NPOs and public enterprises, including issues related to revenue diversification, cost management, and donor relations. Performance measurement and evaluation: This topic covers the measurement and evaluation of performance in NPOs and public enterprises, including issues related to outcome measurement, impact assessment, and social return on investment. Collaboration and partnerships: This topic covers the collaboration and partnership practices of NPOs and public enterprises, including issues related to cross-sectoral partnerships, network management, and stakeholder engagement.

sublevels.name: Tourism Management
sublevels.description: Tourism management is a field within business and management that focuses on managing and developing tourism-related businesses, destinations, and activities. It involves studying and applying strategies to enhance the economic, social, and environmental benefits of tourism. Core topics in tourism management include: Destination management: the planning and management of tourism destinations, including marketing, infrastructure development, and environmental sustainability. Tourism marketing: developing and implementing marketing strategies to promote tourism products and destinations. Hospitality management: managing hotels, resorts, and other hospitality businesses, including customer service, operations, and revenue management. Sustainable tourism: promoting tourism that minimizes negative impacts on the environment and local communities and maximizes positive economic and social benefits.  Cultural tourism: developing and promoting tourism that celebrates local culture, traditions, and heiitage. Tourism economics: analyzing the economic impacts of tourism, including job creation, income generation, and regional development. Tourism policy and planning: developing policies and plans to guide tourism development and management at the local, regional, and national levels. Tourist behavior and experience: understanding tourist motivations, preferences, and behaviors to improve the tourism experience and develop more targeted marketing strategies. Tourism innovation and entrepreneurship: developing new tourism products and services and promoting entrepreneurship and innovation within the tourism industry.

sublevels.name: Fashion Business
sublevels.description: "Fashion Business" refers to the industry and commercial activities involved in the design, production, marketing, and retailing of clothing, accessories, and footwear.

sublevels.name: Public Sector
sublevels.description: The public sector, also called the state sector, is the part of the economy composed of both public services and public enterprises. Public sectors include the public goods and governmental services such as the military, law enforcement, public infrastructure, public transit, public education, along with public health care and those working for the government itself, such as elected officials.

sublevels.name: IT in Business
sublevels.description: IT (Information Technology) in business refers to the use of computer-based technologies to store, process, and transmit information in various forms. ICT (Information and Communication Technology) is a broader term that encompasses both the hardware and software tools used for communication, collaboration, and information management.  As a field of business and management research and practice, IT and ICT cover a wide range of topics, including:  Information systems: This includes the design, development, implementation, and management of information systems such as databases, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, customer relationship management (CRM) systems, and other business intelligence tools.  E-commerce: The use of technology to conduct business transactions over the internet, including online shopping, electronic payments, and digital marketing.  Cybersecurity: The protection of computer systems and networks from theft, damage, or unauthorized access, including topics such as risk management, data privacy, and compliance with regulations.  Digital transformation: The integration of digital technology into all areas of a business, including business processes, customer experience, and organizational culture.  Cloud computing: The use of remote servers to store, manage, and process data, which can provide benefits such as scalability, flexibility, and cost savings.  Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning: The use of algorithms and statistical models to analyze and make predictions based on large data sets.  Mobile computing: The use of mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets to access and share information.  Social media: The use of social networking sites, blogs, and other online platforms for marketing, customer engagement, and brand management.  Overall, IT and ICT are critical components of modern business and management, and research in this field continues to explore new ways to leverage technology to improve organizational performance, enhance customer experience, and drive innovation. This topic deals with all aspects of information technology in business and management processes, including strategy development, digitalization, digital transformation. Business IT infrastructure, information systems, process management, e-business, enterprise architecture and software management are the core sub-topics.

sublevels.name: Enterprise Architecture
sublevels.description: Enterprise Architecture (EA) is a field of business and management research and practice that focuses on the design and implementation of a coherent and integrated set of business and IT capabilities that support an organization's goals and objectives. It involves the development of a comprehensive understanding of an organization's current and desired states, and the identification of the gaps and opportunities for improvement.  The following are major topics within the field of Enterprise Architecture:  Business Architecture: Business Architecture defines the organization's business strategy, goals, processes, and organizational structure. It aims to provide a clear understanding of the organization's operations and how they can be optimized.  Information Architecture: Information Architecture defines the organization's information strategy, including the data, information, and knowledge assets required to support the business processes. It ensures that information is available, secure, and usable by the organization's stakeholders.  Application Architecture: Application Architecture focuses on the design and implementation of software applications that support the organization's business processes. It includes the development of application standards, guidelines, and best practices.  Technology Architecture: Technology Architecture defines the organization's technology strategy, including the hardware, software, and network infrastructure required to support the business processes. It ensures that the technology is aligned with the organization's goals and objectives.  Governance: Governance refers to the establishment of policies, standards, and procedures to ensure that the Enterprise Architecture is consistent with the organization's goals and objectives. It ensures that the organization's resources are used effectively and efficiently.  Change Management: Change Management refers to the process of managing the changes to the Enterprise Architecture. It involves the development of a plan to manage the implementation of new systems, applications, or processes, and the communication of the changes to stakeholders.  Risk Management: Risk Management involves identifying, assessing, and managing risks associated with the implementation of the Enterprise Architecture. It ensures that the organization's assets are protected and that the risks are managed effectively.  Overall, the goal of Enterprise Architecture is to provide a holistic and integrated view of the organization, its processes, and its resources.

sublevels.name: Management
sublevels.description: Define General Management as a field of management research General management is a field of management research that focuses on the overall administration and coordination of all the activities within an organization. It involves the use of various management techniques, principles, and strategies to achieve organizational goals and objectives.  General management encompasses various functions, including planning, organizing, staffing, directing, and controlling. These functions are performed at different levels of the organization, ranging from top-level executives to front-line supervisors. General management also involves decision-making, problem-solving, and effective communication to ensure the smooth functioning of the organization.  The field of general management research also encompasses various topics, including organizational behavior, leadership, strategic management, entrepreneurship, and innovation. It aims to develop and apply theories, models, and frameworks to improve organizational performance and achieve sustainable competitive advantage.  In summary, general management is a crucial field of management research that focuses on managing all aspects of an organization to achieve its goals and objectives. It plays a vital role in ensuring organizational success and sustainability in a dynamic and ever-changing business environment.

sublevels.name: Business Strategy and Leadership
sublevels.description: Business strategy research is a field of management research that focuses on the development, implementation, and evaluation of strategies that organizations use to achieve their objectives. This field of research examines the various elements that contribute to the success of an organization's strategy, including its competitive positioning, industry dynamics, internal resources and capabilities, and external environment. Business strategy research involves analyzing the strategic decisions made by firms, such as mergers and acquisitions, diversification, market entry, and product innovation. It also examines the role of leadership in shaping and executing strategies, as well as the impact of various organizational structures and cultures on strategy implementation. Research in this field employs various methodologies, including quantitative analysis, case studies, and simulation models. Business strategy researchers often collaborate with practitioners in the field, such as executives and consultants, to develop and test new strategies and approaches. The ultimate goal of business strategy research is to provide insights and guidance for organizations as they navigate complex and dynamic business environments. By understanding the factors that drive successful strategy formulation and implementation, businesses can make informed decisions and achieve sustainable competitive advantage. Leadership research is a field of management research that focuses on understanding and analyzing the various aspects of leadership. This field explores the characteristics, behaviors, and skills that make an effective leader and examines how leaders can inspire and motivate others to achieve organizational goals. Leadership research encompasses a wide range of topics, including leadership styles, leadership theories, leadership development, and leadership effectiveness. Researchers in this field use a variety of research methods, such as surveys, case studies, experiments, and interviews, to explore these topics and gain a deeper understanding of leadership and its impact on organizational outcomes. The findings from leadership research have practical implications for organizations, as they provide insight into how to develop effective leaders, create a positive work culture, and enhance organizational performance. As such, leadership research is an important area of study in management research, and it continues to evolve as new trends and challenges emerge in the business world.

sublevels.name: Market Intelligence
sublevels.description: Market Intelligence is a field of management research that involves gathering, analyzing, and interpreting information about the market, customers, competitors, and industry trends to support strategic decision-making. Market intelligence provides businesses with a comprehensive understanding of their market, which can help them identify new opportunities, mitigate risks, and gain a competitive advantage.  Market intelligence is a systematic and ongoing process that involves collecting and analyzing data from a variety of sources, including market research reports, customer surveys, industry publications, and competitor analysis. This information is then used to develop insights and recommendations that guide business strategy and inform decision-making across a range of functions, including product development, marketing, sales, and operations.  The ultimate goal of market intelligence is to provide businesses with a deep understanding of their market and customers, allowing them to make informed decisions that lead to long-term success and profitability. By staying on top of market trends and changes, businesses can adapt quickly to changing conditions and maintain a competitive edge in their industry

sublevels.name: Knowledge Management
sublevels.description: Knowledge Management (KM) is the practice of capturing, creating, sharing, and utilizing knowledge within an organization to achieve its goals and objectives. It is an interdisciplinary field of management research that combines aspects of information technology, organizational theory, psychology, and sociology to develop strategies and tools for managing knowledge effectively.  KM involves the identification, acquisition, creation, distribution, and use of knowledge, as well as the processes and technologies that support these activities. The ultimate goal of KM is to enable an organization to leverage its knowledge assets to improve performance, innovation, and competitiveness.  Some key aspects of KM include knowledge creation, knowledge sharing, and knowledge retention. These activities require a culture that promotes knowledge sharing and collaboration, as well as the use of information technologies that support the management of knowledge.  Overall, KM is a critical field of management research because it enables organizations to leverage their knowledge assets to create value, innovate, and remain competitive in a rapidly changing business environment.

sublevels.name: Management Education
sublevels.description: Management education refers to the study of how to educate and develop effective managers, leaders, and executives. It is a subfield of management research that focuses on identifying best practices in teaching, learning, and curriculum design for management students. Major topics in management education include: Curriculum design and development: This involves designing and developing courses and programs that equip students with the skills and knowledge they need to succeed in their careers as managers and leaders. Teaching and learning methods: This includes identifying and evaluating different teaching and learning methods, such as case studies, experiential learning, simulations, and online learning, and determining which methods are most effective for different types of students and learning objectives. Assessment and evaluation: This involves developing and implementing effective methods for assessing student learning and evaluating the effectiveness of management education programs. Faculty development: This includes identifying and providing training and support for faculty members to ensure they have the skills and knowledge needed to deliver effective management education. Diversity and inclusion: This involves promoting diversity and inclusion in management education by ensuring that courses and programs are designed to address the needs of students from diverse backgrounds and by promoting diversity among faculty and staff. Ethics and corporate social responsibility: This includes developing courses and programs that address ethical issues and promote corporate social responsibility in management education.  Internationalization: This involves preparing students to work in a globalized world by incorporating international perspectives into management education and providing opportunities for students to study and work abroad. Career development: This includes providing students with the skills and knowledge they need to succeed in their careers as managers and leaders, including networking, job search strategies, and career planning.

sublevels.name: Organization
sublevels.description: Organizational research is a field of management research that focuses on understanding the structure, behavior, and performance of organizations. It involves the study of various aspects of organizations, such as their culture, communication patterns, power dynamics, decision-making processes, and leadership styles. The ultimate goal of organizational research is to identify ways to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of organizations. Some of the major topics in organizational research include: Organizational behavior: This involves the study of how individuals, groups, and structures within an organization interact with each other. Topics in organizational behavior include motivation, communication, power, conflict, and leadership. Organizational culture: This involves the study of the values, beliefs, and norms that shape the behavior of individuals within an organization. Topics in organizational culture include the role of rituals and symbols, cultural diversity, and the impact of culture on organizational performance. Human resource management: This involves the study of how organizations manage their employees, including recruitment, training, performance appraisal, and compensation. Topics in human resource management include diversity, employee engagement, and the impact of HR practices on organizational performance. Organizational structure and design: This involves the study of how organizations are structured and designed to achieve their goals. Topics in organizational structure and design include organizational size and complexity, formalization, centralization, and decentralization. Strategic management: This involves the study of how organizations develop and implement strategies to achieve their goals. Topics in strategic management include competitive advantage, innovation, and corporate social responsibility. Organizational change and development: This involves the study of how organizations adapt to changing environments and improve their performance over time. Topics in organizational change and development include organizational learning, change management, and innovation.

sublevels.name: Industrial Psychology
sublevels.description: Industrial psychology, also known as industrial-organizational psychology or I-O psychology, is a field of psychology that focuses on understanding and improving human behavior in the workplace. It applies psychological principles and research methods to address issues related to personnel selection, employee training and development, organizational effectiveness, and work environment. Industrial psychology aims to enhance employee well-being, productivity, and job satisfaction while optimizing organizational performance and efficiency.

sublevels.name: Project Management
sublevels.description: Project management is the process of planning, executing, monitoring, and controlling the work of a team to achieve specific goals and objectives within a defined timeline and budget. It involves applying knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to manage project activities effectively and efficiently. The major components of project management are: Project Scope: The objectives, deliverables, and requirements that define the project's boundaries. Project Schedule: The timeline for completing the project, including specific deadlines for milestones and deliverables. Project Budget: The estimated cost of resources needed to complete the project, including personnel, equipment, and materials. Project Team: The group of individuals responsible for completing the project. Project Communication: The process of sharing information with stakeholders and team members to ensure everyone is aware of project status, changes, and expectations. Project Risk Management: The process of identifying, assessing, and mitigating potential risks that could impact the project's success. Major methodologies and standards used in project management include: Agile: An iterative approach to project management that emphasizes flexibility and collaboration among team members. Waterfall: A linear approach to project management that involves completing tasks in a sequential manner, with each phase dependent on the completion of the previous one. Scrum: An Agile framework for managing and completing complex projects by breaking them down into smaller, more manageable tasks. Lean: A methodology that focuses on maximizing value while minimizing waste, by streamlining processes and eliminating unnecessary steps. PRINCE2: A process-based project management methodology that emphasizes control, governance, and risk management. PMBOK: The Project Management Body of Knowledge, developed by the Project Management Institute (PMI), is a collection of best practices and guidelines for project management.

sublevels.name: Marketing
sublevels.description: Marketing research is a crucial component of business and management research that involves the systematic collection and analysis of data related to a company's marketing activities. It is the process of gathering, analyzing, and interpreting data to gain insights into customer behavior, market trends, and competitive landscape to help businesses make informed decisions about their marketing strategies. Marketing research involves various methods and techniques, including surveys, focus groups, interviews, observation, and data analysis tools. The research can be conducted for different purposes such as product development, pricing strategies, customer satisfaction, brand awareness, and market segmentation. Overall, marketing research plays a crucial role in helping companies understand their customers' needs and preferences, identify potential opportunities and challenges in the market, and make informed decisions to achieve their business objectives.

sublevels.name: Customer Relationship Management
sublevels.description: Consumer Relationship Management (CRM) is a business strategy that focuses on managing interactions and relationships with customers in order to maximize their lifetime value to the company. CRM involves the use of technology and data analysis to identify and target customers, as well as to personalize and enhance their experiences with the company.  At its core, CRM involves building a deep understanding of each customer's needs, preferences, and behaviors, and using this knowledge to tailor the company's products, services, and communications to meet those needs. This involves collecting and analyzing data from multiple sources, including customer interactions, social media, and other sources, to gain insights into customer behavior and preferences.  Effective CRM can lead to increased customer satisfaction, loyalty, and retention, as well as improved sales and revenue growth for the company. It requires a coordinated effort across multiple departments and functions within the organization, including marketing, sales, customer service, and IT.

sublevels.name: Branding
sublevels.description: Branding is the process of creating a unique and identifiable name, symbol, design, or image that represents a company, product, or service. It is a fundamental aspect of marketing that helps to differentiate a company from its competitors, build customer loyalty, and increase brand recognition. Brand strategy, on the other hand, refers to the long-term plan or roadmap that guides the development and management of a brand. It involves defining the brand's positioning, target audience, messaging, and marketing tactics, as well as measuring and optimizing the brand's performance over time.

sublevels.name: Digital Marketing
sublevels.description: Digital marketing is a branch of marketing that utilizes digital technologies and channels to promote and advertise products or services to potential customers. It involves a range of activities, including but not limited to, search engine optimization (SEO), social media marketing, email marketing, content marketing, paid advertising, and mobile marketing.  In management research, digital marketing is studied as a strategic approach to reaching and engaging with customers in an increasingly digital world. It examines how businesses can leverage digital technologies and channels to create more targeted and effective marketing campaigns, build stronger relationships with customers, and ultimately drive sales and revenue growth.  Researchers in this field explore topics such as consumer behavior in digital environments, the impact of social media on customer engagement, the effectiveness of different digital marketing channels, and the role of data analytics in measuring marketing effectiveness. They also examine the challenges and opportunities associated with digital marketing, such as managing customer privacy and data security, staying up-to-date with evolving technologies, and balancing online and offline marketing efforts.

sublevels.name: Market Research and Competitive Intelligence
sublevels.description: Market research refers to the systematic gathering and analysis of information about a particular market or industry to understand customers, competitors, and market trends. It involves identifying customer needs, preferences, and behaviors, as well as evaluating market opportunities, challenges, and threats.  Competitive intelligence, on the other hand, is the process of collecting and analyzing information about a company's competitors, including their strengths, weaknesses, strategies, and market positioning. Competitive intelligence helps businesses to understand their competitive landscape, identify potential threats and opportunities, and make strategic decisions.  Both market research and competitive intelligence are important components of management research. They provide valuable insights that can help businesses make informed decisions about product development, marketing, pricing, distribution, and other business strategies. By conducting market research and competitive intelligence, businesses can stay ahead of the competition, identify new market opportunities, and improve their overall performance.

sublevels.name: Consumer Behavior
sublevels.description: Consumer behavior refers to the study of individuals, groups, or organizations and the processes they use to select, secure, use, and dispose of products, services, experiences, or ideas to satisfy their needs and desires. It is a crucial area of research for management as it helps companies understand their customers better and develop marketing strategies to meet their needs effectively.  Consumer behavior research involves analyzing various factors that influence consumers' buying decisions, including their psychological, social, cultural, and economic factors. It helps companies understand the motivations, attitudes, and preferences of their customers and how these factors influence their buying decisions.  By understanding consumer behavior, companies can create products and services that better meet their customers' needs, develop effective marketing campaigns, and build stronger relationships with their customers. It also helps companies identify potential new markets and opportunities for growth.

sublevels.name: Media Planning
sublevels.description: Media planning is a crucial component of marketing and advertising that involves developing a strategic plan to reach and engage with a target audience through various media channels. This process typically involves researching the target audience to understand their interests, behaviors, and preferences, as well as identifying the most effective media channels to reach them.  Media planning often involves working with media buyers and vendors to negotiate pricing and placement of advertisements across various media platforms, such as television, radio, print, digital, and social media. The goal of media planning is to develop a comprehensive media strategy that maximizes the impact of advertising and marketing efforts while minimizing costs.  In management research, media planning is often studied as a way to understand how organizations can effectively allocate resources towards advertising and marketing initiatives, and how they can measure the impact of these initiatives on overall business performance. Researchers may investigate the effectiveness of different media channels, the role of audience targeting and segmentation, and the use of metrics to measure advertising effectiveness and return on investment.

sublevels.name: Operations Research and Decision Theory
sublevels.description: Operations Research (OR) is a field of management research and practice that uses mathematical modeling, statistical analysis, and optimization techniques to solve complex problems in organizations. The primary objective of OR is to improve decision-making processes and the overall efficiency and effectiveness of organizations. OR involves the application of various techniques such as linear programming, network analysis, queuing theory, simulation, and decision analysis to support decision-making processes.  Decision Theory, on the other hand, is a field of management research and practice that focuses on understanding and improving the decision-making process. Decision theory provides a framework for analyzing and evaluating decisions under conditions of uncertainty and risk. It involves the use of mathematical models and methods to identify the best course of action based on available information, preferences, and outcomes. Decision theory is used in a wide range of applications, including business, economics, psychology, and political science.  Both OR and Decision Theory are interdisciplinary fields that draw on knowledge from mathematics, computer science, economics, psychology, and other disciplines. They are widely used in various domains, including manufacturing, logistics, finance, healthcare, and transportation, to name a few. By providing a scientific approach to decision-making, OR and Decision Theory help organizations make better-informed decisions and achieve their goals more effectively.

sublevels.name: Human Resource Management
sublevels.description: Human Resource Management (HRM) is a field of research and practice that focuses on managing people in organizations. It involves the strategic planning, recruitment, selection, development, motivation, and retention of employees to achieve organizational goals and objectives. As a field of research, HRM studies focus on understanding the theoretical and practical aspects of managing people in organizations. Research topics may include recruitment and selection, training and development, performance management, compensation and benefits, employee relations, and legal compliance. Researchers in HRM aim to provide evidence-based insights that can inform the development of effective HR policies and practices in organizations. As a field of practice, HRM involves designing and implementing strategies, policies, and practices to attract, develop, motivate, and retain employees. HR professionals are responsible for managing a wide range of HR functions, including talent acquisition, performance management, training and development, compensation and benefits, and employee relations. They work closely with other functional areas of the organization to align HR strategies with overall business goals and objectives. Overall, HRM is an important field of research and practice as it contributes to the development of effective and sustainable HR strategies that can enhance organizational performance, employee engagement, and overall well-being.

sublevels.name: Human Resource Development
sublevels.description: Human Resource Development (HRD) is a field of research and practice that focuses on the training, development, and education of employees in organizations. HRD professionals work to improve the skills, knowledge, and abilities of employees through a variety of interventions, including training programs, performance management, coaching, and mentoring. In research, HRD examines how organizations can develop and implement effective training and development programs to enhance employee skills and competencies. Researchers in this field explore topics such as adult learning, instructional design, employee motivation, and the use of technology in training and development. In practice, HRD professionals work with organizations to identify skills gaps and training needs, and develop programs to address them. They may also provide coaching and mentoring services to employees, or work with managers to improve performance management processes. HRD professionals are often involved in talent management initiatives, such as succession planning and leadership development, to ensure that organizations have the skills and capabilities they need to achieve their strategic objectives.

sublevels.name: Organizational Learning
sublevels.description: Organizational learning is a field of research that focuses on how organizations acquire, process, and use knowledge to improve their performance and achieve their goals. It involves studying the ways in which organizations learn from their experiences, both positive and negative, and how they use this knowledge to adapt to changing environments, innovate, and improve their practices and processes. The main topics within organizational learning include: Knowledge acquisition: This refers to how organizations gather and collect knowledge from various sources, such as employees, customers, suppliers, and competitors. This involves understanding the mechanisms and processes of knowledge creation, transfer, and sharing. Knowledge transfer and sharing: This refers to the ways in which organizations share knowledge within and across different units or departments. It involves studying the communication, collaboration, and coordination processes that facilitate knowledge transfer and sharing. Learning processes: This refers to the cognitive and behavioral processes that individuals and groups use to acquire and use knowledge. This involves studying how individuals and groups process information, make decisions, and learn from their experiences. Organizational culture and climate: This refers to the shared values, norms, beliefs, and practices that shape the learning environment within an organization. It involves studying how the organizational culture and climate can facilitate or inhibit learning. Innovation and creativity: This refers to the ways in which organizations use their knowledge to innovate and create new products, services, and processes. It involves studying the mechanisms and processes of innovation, such as idea generation, experimentation, and implementation. Performance improvement: This refers to the ways in which organizations use their knowledge to improve their performance and achieve their goals. It involves studying the mechanisms and processes of performance improvement, such as benchmarking, continuous improvement, and knowledge management.

sublevels.name: Employee Health and Wellbeing
sublevels.description: Employee health and wellbeing is a field of research and practice that focuses on improving the physical, mental, and emotional health of employees in the workplace. It involves designing and implementing programs, policies, and practices that promote employee health and wellbeing, such as wellness programs, stress management initiatives, mental health support, and flexible work arrangements. In research, the field explores the impact of work-related factors on employee health and wellbeing, as well as the effectiveness of different interventions in improving employee health outcomes. Researchers also examine the business benefits of promoting employee health and wellbeing, such as reduced healthcare costs, increased productivity, and improved employee engagement and retention. In practice, employee health and wellbeing professionals work with employers to develop and implement programs and policies that support employee health and wellbeing. They may also provide individual coaching and counseling services to employees to help them manage stress, improve their mental health, and adopt healthy lifestyle habits.

sublevels.name: Careers in Business and Management
sublevels.description: The field of careers in business and management encompasses research and practice related to the study and management of careers within the context of organizations. It focuses on understanding how individuals can build successful and satisfying careers within the business and management field, as well as how organizations can attract, retain, and develop talent.  As a field of research, careers in business and management explores various topics such as career development, career success, career transitions, career mobility, and career management practices within organizations. Research in this area seeks to identify factors that contribute to career success and satisfaction, such as work-life balance, job fit, organizational culture, and leadership practices.  As a field of practice, careers in business and management involves designing and implementing programs and practices that support employee career development and enhance organizational talent management. This includes providing training and development opportunities, creating career paths, implementing performance management systems, and fostering a supportive organizational culture that values employee career growth and development.  Overall, careers in business and management is an important field that contributes to the development of effective talent management practices and supports the growth and success of individuals and organizations in the business and management field.

sublevels.name: Entrepreneurship
sublevels.description: Entrepreneurship as a field of research refers to the study of the processes, activities, and behaviors that lead to the creation and growth of new ventures. It involves examining the factors that influence the success or failure of entrepreneurial activities and identifying best practices and strategies for starting and growing successful businesses.  In entrepreneurship research, scholars and practitioners study a wide range of topics, including:  Opportunity recognition and evaluation: How do entrepreneurs identify and evaluate business opportunities, and what factors influence their decision-making?  Innovation and creativity: How do entrepreneurs come up with new and innovative ideas for products, services, and business models, and what role does creativity play in the entrepreneurial process?  Entrepreneurial finance: What are the sources of capital for new ventures, and how can entrepreneurs access the funding they need to start and grow their businesses?  Entrepreneurial marketing: How do entrepreneurs market and sell their products and services, and what marketing strategies are most effective for new ventures?  Entrepreneurial leadership: What are the leadership styles and behaviors that are most effective in the context of entrepreneurial activities, and how can entrepreneurs develop these skills?  Overall, entrepreneurship as a field of research seeks to understand the processes, behaviors, and strategies that lead to successful entrepreneurship, and to develop practical recommendations for entrepreneurs and policymakers to support the creation and growth of new ventures.

sublevels.name: Start-Ups and Venture Capital
sublevels.description: Start-up, venture capital, and business angel are related terms in the field of entrepreneurship, which involves starting and growing new businesses.  Start-up refers to a newly founded business enterprise that is typically characterized by a high degree of innovation, uncertainty, and risk. Start-ups are often founded by entrepreneurs who have a novel business idea or technology and seek to commercialize it. As a field of research, start-up studies focus on the process of starting and growing new businesses, including issues such as opportunity identification, business planning, funding, team building, and scaling.  Venture capital (VC) is a form of private equity financing that provides funding to start-ups and early-stage companies that have high growth potential. VC investors provide funding to start-ups in exchange for an ownership stake in the company, and they typically take an active role in managing the company's growth and development. As a field of research, venture capital studies focus on the investment process, including issues such as investment criteria, portfolio management, and exit strategies.  Business angel (also known as angel investor) is an individual investor who provides funding to start-ups in exchange for an ownership stake in the company. Business angels are typically high net worth individuals who have industry expertise and are willing to take a high degree of risk in exchange for potentially high returns. As a field of research, business angel studies focus on the characteristics and behaviors of angel investors, as well as the impact of business angel funding on start-up success.  Overall, start-up, venture capital, and business angel are important fields of research and practice in the entrepreneurship ecosystem, as they support the development and growth of new businesses, drive innovation, and contribute to economic development.

sublevels.name: Small Business
sublevels.description: Small business or SME (small and medium-sized enterprises) research refers to the study of businesses that have relatively small size, limited resources, and a narrow scope of operations. SMEs are often seen as the backbone of the economy, as they play a vital role in job creation, innovation, and economic growth. In small business or SME research, scholars and practitioners study a wide range of topics, including: Entrepreneurship and innovation: What are the factors that influence the creation and success of small businesses, and how can entrepreneurs leverage innovation to achieve growth and competitiveness? Financing and capital access: What are the financing challenges faced by small businesses, and how can they access the funding they need to start and grow their businesses? Marketing and sales: How can small businesses effectively market their products and services, and build customer relationships that lead to long-term success? Human resource management: How can small businesses attract and retain talented employees, and build effective teams that support business growth? Technology and digitalization: How can small businesses leverage technology and digitalization to increase efficiency, improve customer experiences, and compete with larger firms? Small business management refers to the process of planning, organizing, leading, and controlling resources (including people, finances, and operations) in a small business setting to achieve specific goals and objectives. Small business management involves making strategic decisions about the allocation of resources, developing and implementing operational plans, monitoring performance, and adapting to changing circumstances.

sublevels.name: Microfinance
sublevels.description:
Microfinance refers to the financial services provided to low-income individuals or groups who are typically excluded from traditional banking. Most microfinance institutions focus on offering credit in the form of small working capital loans, sometimes called microloans or microcredit. However, many also provide insurance and money transfers, and regulated microfinance banks provide savings accounts.

Microfinance aims to improve financial services access for marginalized groups, especially women and the rural poor, to promote self-sufficiency.

sublevels.name: Family Business
sublevels.description: Family Business is a field of research that focuses on the unique characteristics and dynamics of businesses that are owned and operated by families. It involves the study of the intersection between family and business systems, and the ways in which these systems influence the performance, management, and governance of family-owned businesses.  In family business research, scholars and practitioners study a wide range of topics, including:  Family dynamics: How do family dynamics, such as family roles, power structures, and communication patterns, affect the performance and management of family-owned businesses?  Succession planning: How do family-owned businesses plan for the transition of leadership and ownership from one generation to the next, and what factors influence the success or failure of these transitions?  Governance and management: What are the best practices for governance and management in family-owned businesses, and how can families balance the needs of the business with the needs of the family?  Inter-generational entrepreneurship: What are the factors that influence the success or failure of inter-generational entrepreneurship within family-owned businesses?  Family business financing: What are the unique financing challenges faced by family-owned businesses, and how can they access the funding they need to grow and succeed?  Overall, family business research seeks to understand the complex interplay between family and business systems in family-owned businesses, and to develop practical recommendations for families and practitioners to improve the performance, management, and governance of these businesses.

sublevels.name: Creative Industries
sublevels.description: Creative industries are those industries which have their origin in individual creativity, skill and talent which have a potential for job and wealth creation through the generation and exploitation of intellectual property"Examples of creative industries include music, the arts and theatre.

sublevels.name: Innovation and Technology Management
sublevels.description: Innovation and Technology Management is a field within business and management that focuses on developing, implementing, and managing innovative technologies and processes in organizations. It involves the management of technology, research and development, product development, and commercialization of technology. The core topics within Innovation and Technology Management include: Innovation strategy: This involves the formulation of strategies for the development, acquisition, and commercialization of innovative products and technologies. Technology management: This includes the management of technology resources, technology planning, technology development, and technology transfer. Research and development: This includes the development and management of research and development processes, research and development teams, and research and development budgets. Intellectual property: This includes the identification, protection, and exploitation of intellectual property rights, such as patents, trademarks, and copyrights. Commercialization: This includes the development of strategies and processes for bringing new products and technologies to market, including marketing, sales, and distribution.  Open innovation: This includes the development of partnerships and collaborations with external organizations for the sharing of knowledge, resources, and expertise. Entrepreneurship: This includes the development of new ventures and the management of innovation-based startups. Organizational innovation: This includes the development of innovative processes and practices within organizations, such as new organizational structures, work processes, and communication systems. Digital transformation: This involves the integration of digital technologies into organizational processes and operations to increase efficiency and competitiveness.

sublevels.name: Technology Commercialization
sublevels.description: Technology commercialization is a field within business and management research and practice that focuses on the process of bringing new technological innovations to the market. It involves the transformation of technological inventions into marketable products or services. Core topics within technology commercialization include: Intellectual property protection: This involves protecting the legal rights of the inventor or organization that owns the technology. Market analysis: This involves analyzing the market potential for the new technology and identifying potential customers and competitors. Business models: This involves identifying the most effective business models for commercializing the technology, such as licensing or direct sales. Funding and financing: This involves identifying and securing funding and financing for the commercialization process, including venture capital, grants, and loans. Product development: This involves developing and testing prototypes of the new technology, refining its features, and ensuring that it meets the needs of the market. Marketing and sales: This involves developing a marketing strategy for the new technology and identifying the most effective sales channels. Entrepreneurship and innovation: This involves understanding the entrepreneurial and innovative aspects of the commercialization process, including the role of entrepreneurship in driving technological innovation and the importance of creating a culture of innovation within organizations.

sublevels.name: Licensing
sublevels.description: Licensing refers to the legal process of granting permission to use an intellectual property (IP) asset such as a patent, trademark, or copyright to a third party in exchange for compensation, usually in the form of royalties or fees. Licensing is an important field of research and practice within technology commercialization because it enables companies to monetize their inventions and innovations while avoiding the costs and risks associated with manufacturing and distribution. The core topics of licensing as a field of research and practice within technology commercialization include: Intellectual Property Law: Licensing is a legal process, and thus a fundamental understanding of intellectual property law is essential for practitioners in this field. This includes knowledge of the different types of IP assets, the requirements for obtaining and maintaining them, and the legal frameworks that govern their use and enforcement.  Negotiation and Contracting: Licensing agreements involve complex negotiations and contractual agreements between the licensor and the licensee. Practitioners must be skilled in drafting and negotiating these agreements, as well as understanding the key terms and provisions that are critical to the success of the licensing deal. Technology Assessment: Before licensing a technology, it is important to assess its commercial viability and potential market demand. Practitioners must be able to evaluate the technology's potential market size, competitive landscape, and potential applications to determine whether it is a viable candidate for licensing. Market Analysis: To successfully license a technology, practitioners must have a deep understanding of the market and the competitive landscape. This includes conducting market research, identifying potential licensees, and developing a licensing strategy that aligns with the company's overall business goals. Intellectual Property Valuation: Determining the value of an IP asset is critical in negotiating licensing agreements. Practitioners must be able to accurately assess the value of the IP asset, taking into account factors such as the strength of the patent, the size of the market, and the potential revenue streams. Compliance and Enforcement: Once a licensing agreement is in place, it is important to ensure that both parties comply with the terms of the agreement. Practitioners must be able to monitor and enforce compliance, and take legal action when necessary to protect the licensor's rights and interests. Overall, licensing is a complex field that requires a deep understanding of intellectual property law, negotiation and contracting, technology assessment, market analysis, intellectual property valuation, and compliance and enforcement.

sublevels.name: Patenting
sublevels.description: Patenting is a field of management research and practice that focuses on the strategic use of patents to commercialize technology. This field encompasses a range of topics related to the identification, acquisition, management, and enforcement of patents in order to create value for a firm.  Core topics within the field of patenting include:  Patent strategy: This topic focuses on developing a patent strategy that aligns with a firm's overall business goals. It involves understanding the competitive landscape and identifying areas where patents can be used to create a competitive advantage.  Patent acquisition: This topic deals with the process of acquiring patents either through internal development or external sources, such as licensing or purchasing patents from other firms. It includes assessing the value of patents and negotiating licensing or acquisition agreements.  Patent portfolio management: This topic involves managing a firm's patent portfolio to maximize its value. It includes identifying and prioritizing patents for commercialization, monitoring the patent landscape for potential infringement, and assessing the potential value of new patents.  Patent litigation: This topic deals with the legal aspects of enforcing patents, such as filing lawsuits against infringers or defending against infringement claims. It includes assessing the likelihood of success in litigation and the potential costs and benefits of pursuing legal action.  Patent licensing: This topic involves negotiating licensing agreements with other firms to commercialize patented technology. It includes assessing the value of the licensed technology, negotiating licensing terms, and monitoring compliance with the licensing agreement.  Overall, patenting is a critical field for firms looking to commercialize technology, and understanding its core topics is essential for success in this area.

sublevels.name: Academic Spin-Offs
sublevels.description: Academic spin-offs refer to new ventures that are created to commercialize technologies, products, or services developed in universities or research institutions. These ventures are typically founded by academic researchers or entrepreneurs who have a strong knowledge of the technology and market opportunities for their innovation.  The field of academic spin-offs encompasses a range of research and practice areas, including:  Technology transfer: This involves the transfer of knowledge, intellectual property, and technology from universities or research institutions to new ventures. It includes issues such as patenting, licensing, and protecting intellectual property.  Entrepreneurship: This includes the skills and competencies required to start and grow a new venture. It includes topics such as business planning, fundraising, and marketing.  Innovation management: This involves the processes and strategies for managing innovation within a new venture. It includes topics such as product development, market research, and project management.  Financing and funding: This involves the sources of funding and financing available for academic spin-offs. It includes topics such as venture capital, angel investing, and crowdfunding.  Legal and regulatory issues: This involves the legal and regulatory frameworks that impact academic spin-offs. It includes topics such as corporate governance, securities regulations, and tax laws.  Overall, the field of academic spin-offs is interdisciplinary, encompassing business, technology, law, and policy. It is an important area of research and practice, as it provides a pathway for bringing new technologies and innovations to market, creating jobs, and driving economic growth.

sublevels.name: Corporate Finance
sublevels.description: Define "Corporate Finance" as in Research and Practice Corporate finance is a field of finance that deals with the financial and investment decisions of corporations. It involves managing the financial resources of a company to maximize shareholder value, while taking into account factors such as risk, cost of capital, and financial performance.  In research and practice, corporate finance encompasses a wide range of topics, including:  Capital budgeting: The process of making investment decisions that involve long-term assets and projects.  Capital structure: The mix of debt and equity financing used to fund a company's operations and growth.  Risk management: The identification, assessment, and mitigation of risks that may impact a company's financial performance.  Corporate valuation: The process of determining the value of a company, its assets, and its investments.  Financial analysis: The process of analyzing a company's financial statements to evaluate its financial performance and make investment decisions.  Mergers and acquisitions: The process of buying, selling, or combining companies to create synergies and improve financial performance.  Corporate governance: The system of rules, practices, and processes by which a company is directed and controlled, including the roles and responsibilities of board members, management, and shareholders.  Dividend policy: The decision of whether to distribute earnings to shareholders in the form of dividends or retain earnings for future investments.  Financial reporting: The process of preparing and disclosing financial information to stakeholders, including financial statements and other disclosures.  Overall, the goal of corporate finance is to create value for shareholders by making effective financial decisions and managing financial risks.

sublevels.name: Entrepreneurial Finance
sublevels.description: Entrepreneurial finance refers to the financial activities and decisions involved in starting and growing a new venture. In research and practice, it is a subfield of finance that focuses specifically on the unique challenges and opportunities of financing new businesses. Entrepreneurial finance involves a wide range of activities and decisions, including: Raising capital: Entrepreneurs need to raise capital to start and grow their businesses. This may involve seeking funding from friends and family, angel investors, venture capitalists, or other sources of financing. Financial planning and forecasting: Entrepreneurs must develop financial plans and forecasts that outline their business goals and projections for revenue, expenses, and cash flow. Capital structure decisions: Entrepreneurs must make decisions about the mix of debt and equity financing they will use to fund their businesses, as well as the terms of these financing arrangements. Managing risk: Entrepreneurs face a wide range of financial risks, including market risk, credit risk, and operational risk. They must develop strategies to manage these risks and ensure the financial stability of their businesses. Exit strategies: Entrepreneurs must develop exit strategies that outline how they will exit their businesses and generate returns for investors, whether through an initial public offering (IPO), acquisition, or other means. Overall, entrepreneurial finance is a critical component of starting and growing a successful new venture. By understanding the unique financial challenges and opportunities of entrepreneurship, entrepreneurs and investors can make informed decisions that increase the chances of success.

sublevels.name: Financial Technology and Innovation
sublevels.description: Financial technology, or fintech, refers to the use of technology to improve and automate financial services and transactions. Fintech companies use innovative technologies such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, and machine learning to provide new financial services or improve existing ones. In research and practice, fintech and innovation involve a range of activities and tasks, including:  Development of new financial products and services: Fintech companies are constantly developing new financial products and services, such as mobile payments, robo-advisors, and peer-to-peer lending platforms, that offer more convenience, accessibility, and affordability than traditional financial services.  Improving financial processes: Fintech companies are also focused on improving financial processes such as underwriting, credit scoring, and fraud detection, by leveraging advanced data analytics and machine learning algorithms.  Enhancing customer experience: Fintech companies use digital channels and user-friendly interfaces to provide a seamless and personalized customer experience, which is a key differentiator in the competitive financial services market.  Increasing financial inclusion: Fintech companies are also focused on increasing financial inclusion, by providing financial services to underserved and unbanked populations, and by offering more affordable and accessible financial services to low-income individuals and small businesses.  Overall, the goal of fintech and innovation is to improve the efficiency, accessibility, and affordability of financial services, and to drive innovation and competition in the financial services industry. In practice, fintech and innovation are transforming the financial services industry, by disrupting traditional business models and creating new opportunities for growth and profitability.

sublevels.name: Mergers and Acquisitions
sublevels.description: Mergers and acquisitions (M&A) refer to the process of combining two or more companies to form a new entity or to acquire another company, respectively. In research and practice, M&A involves a range of activities and tasks, including:  Strategic planning: This involves identifying potential acquisition targets or merger partners, evaluating the strategic fit, and developing a strategy for the M&A transaction.  Due diligence: This involves conducting a thorough investigation of the target company's financial, legal, operational, and strategic aspects to identify any potential risks, liabilities, or opportunities associated with the transaction.  Valuation: This involves assessing the value of the target company, using various methods such as discounted cash flow analysis, comparable company analysis, or precedent transactions analysis, to determine the purchase price or exchange ratio for the transaction.  Negotiation and structuring: This involves negotiating the terms and conditions of the transaction, such as the purchase price, payment method, and post-merger management structure, and structuring the deal to minimize risks and maximize synergies.  Integration planning and execution: This involves planning and executing the integration of the two companies, including aligning business processes and systems, integrating cultures and management teams, and realizing synergies and cost savings.  Overall, the goal of M&A is to create value for the shareholders of the acquiring company, by expanding the business, entering new markets, or achieving cost savings through economies of scale. In practice, M&A is used by a range of organizations, including corporations, private equity firms, and investment banks, to achieve their strategic objectives and grow their businesses.

sublevels.name: Investment Appraisal
sublevels.description: Investment appraisal, also known as capital budgeting, refers to the process of evaluating and selecting long-term investment projects or proposals, based on their potential to generate returns or create value for the organization. In research and practice, investment appraisal involves a range of techniques and methods for analyzing and evaluating investment opportunities, including: Net present value (NPV) analysis: This involves calculating the present value of the expected cash flows generated by the investment, and subtracting the initial investment cost. If the NPV is positive, the investment is considered viable. Internal rate of return (IRR) analysis: This involves calculating the rate of return that the investment is expected to generate, based on the expected cash flows. If the IRR is higher than the organization's cost of capital, the investment is considered viable. Payback period analysis: This involves calculating the length of time it will take for the investment to generate enough cash flows to recover the initial investment cost. If the payback period is shorter than the organization's investment horizon, the investment is considered viable. Sensitivity analysis: This involves testing the impact of changes in key assumptions, such as sales volumes, costs, or discount rates, on the viability of the investment.
