sublevels.description: It is a type of mathematics which use formulas and data to help solve problems in industry, academia, and government.

sublevels.name: Mathematical Applications in Chemistry
sublevels.description: Mathematical chemistry is the area of research engaged in novel applications of mathematics to chemistry; it concerns itself principally with the mathematical modeling of chemical phenomena. Major areas of research in mathematical chemistry include chemical graph theory, which deals with topology such as the mathematical study of isomerism and the development of topological descriptors or indices which find application in quantitative structure-property relationships; and chemical aspects of group theory, which finds applications in stereochemistry and quantum chemistry. Another important area is molecular knot theory and circuit topology that describe the topology of folded linear molecules such as proteins and Nucleic Acids.

sublevels.name: Mathematical Applications in Computer Science
sublevels.description: Mathematical applications are fundamental to computer science, providing the theoretical foundation and practical tools necessary for various aspects of the discipline such as Algorithms and Data Structures, Cryptography, Logic and Formal Methods.

sublevels.name: Information and Communication, Circuits
sublevels.description: Information and Communication Circuits are electronic circuits designed to process and transmit information or signals in communication systems. Information and Communication Circuits are essential components of communication systems, including telecommunications networks, wireless systems, satellite communication, computer networks, and many other applications.

sublevels.name: Discrete Mathematics in Computer Science
sublevels.description: Discrete mathematics plays a fundamental role in computer science. It provides the theoretical foundation and mathematical tools necessary for analyzing and solving problems in various areas of computer science, including algorithms, data structures, cryptography, logic, and computer networks

sublevels.name: Queueing Theory
sublevels.description: Queueing theory is a field of management research and practice that focuses on the study of waiting lines, or queues, and the mathematical models used to analyze them. The goal of queueing theory is to understand the behavior of queues, how to design systems that minimize wait times and improve efficiency, and how to make informed decisions regarding system improvements and resource allocation.  Queueing theory considers various factors that impact queue performance, such as the arrival rate of customers or requests, the service rate of the system, the number of servers or service points available, and the behavior of customers while they wait. By analyzing these factors, queueing theory provides managers and analysts with the tools to optimize system performance, identify bottlenecks, and evaluate system trade-offs.  Queueing theory has broad applications in many fields, including telecommunications, transportation, healthcare, finance, and manufacturing. It is used to design call centers, hospitals, factories, and other systems that require efficient resource utilization and customer service. In addition, queueing theory is also used to study the behavior of customers and employees, providing insights into their decision-making processes and the factors that influence their behavior.

sublevels.name: Numerical Simulation
sublevels.description: A numerical simulation is a calculation that is run on a computer following a program that implements a mathematical model for a physical system. Numerical simulations are required to study the behaviour of systems whose mathematical models are too complex to provide analytical solutions, as in most nonlinear systems.

sublevels.name: Probability and Statistics in Computer Science
sublevels.description: Probability and Statistics for Computer Science treats the most common discrete and continuous distributions, showing how they find use in decision and estimation problems, and constructs computer algorithms for generating observations from the various distributions.

sublevels.name: Mathematical Finance
sublevels.description: Mathematical Finance uses mathematical models and techniques to analyze financial markets, instruments, and risks, providing insights into pricing, investment strategies, and financial decision-making.

sublevels.name: Mathematics in Art and Architecture
sublevels.description: The use of mathematics to plan their blueprints or initial sketch designs also calculate the probability of issues the construction team could run into as they bring the design vision to life in three dimensions.

sublevels.name: Mathematical Models of Cognitive Processes and Neural Networks
sublevels.description: Mathematical models of cognitive processes and neural networks provide a quantitative framework for understanding and simulating the complex behaviors of the brain and the mind. These models aim to capture the underlying mechanisms and dynamics of cognitive processes and neural activity.

sublevels.name: Mathematics in Music
sublevels.description: Counting, rhythm, scales, intervals, patterns, symbols, harmonies, time signatures, overtones, tone, pitch. The notations of composers and sounds made by musicians are connected to mathematics.

sublevels.name: Mathematical Biology
sublevels.description: Mathematical biology or biomathematics is a branch of biology which employs theoretical analysis, mathematical models and abstractions of the living organisms to investigate the principles that govern the structure, development and behavior of the systems, as opposed to experimental biology which deals with the conduction of experiments to prove and validate the scientific theories.

sublevels.name: Analysis
sublevels.description: Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics dealing with limits and related theories, such as differentiation, integration, measure, infinite series, and analytic functions.

sublevels.name: Sequences, Series, Summability
sublevels.description: In mathematics, a series is, roughly speaking, a description of the operation of adding infinitely many quantities, one after the other, to a given starting quantity. Sequences are the basis for series, which are important in differential equations and analysis

sublevels.name: Potential Theory
sublevels.description: Potential theory is the study of harmonic functions

sublevels.name: Functional Analysis
sublevels.description: Functional analysis is a branch of mathematical analysis, the core of which is formed by the study of vector spaces endowed with some kind of limit-related structure (e.g. inner product, norm, topology, etc.) and the linear functions defined on these spaces and respecting these structures in a suitable sense.

sublevels.name: Measure and Integration
sublevels.description: Measure Theory is the study of measures. Measure on a set is a systematic way to assign a number to each suitable subset of that set, intuitively interpreted as its size. In this sense, a measure is a generalization of the concepts of length, area, and volume. Measure theory was developed during the late 19th and early 20th centuries by Émile Borel, Henri Lebesgue, Johann Radon, and Maurice Fréchet, among others. The main applications of measures are in the foundations of the Lebesgue integral, in Andrey Kolmogorov's axiomatisation of probability theory and in ergodic theory. In integration theory, specifying a measure allows one to define integrals on spaces more general than subsets of Euclidean space

sublevels.name: Global Analysis and Analysis on Manifolds
sublevels.description: In mathematics, global analysis, also called analysis on manifolds, is the study of the global and topological properties of differential equations on manifolds and vector bundles. It uses techniques in infinite-dimensional manifold theory and topological spaces of mappings to classify behaviors of differential equations, particularly nonlinear differential equations. These spaces can include singularities and hence catastrophe theory is a part of global analysis. Optimization problems, such as finding geodesics on Riemannian manifolds, can be solved using differential equations so that the calculus of variations overlaps with global analysis.

sublevels.name: Partial Differential Equations on Manifolds
sublevels.description: A manifold is a mathematical space that locally resembles Euclidean space but may have a more complex global structure. PDEs on manifolds are used to describe and analyze various physical, geometric, and differential geometric phenomena that occur on these curved spaces. The formulation of PDEs on manifolds takes into account the geometric properties of the manifold, such as its curvature and metric, which are essential for understanding the behavior of solutions.

sublevels.name: Fourier Analysis
sublevels.description: Is the study of the way general functions may be represented or approximated by sums of simpler trigonometric functions. Fourier analysis grew from the study of Fourier series, and is named after Joseph Fourier, who showed that representing a function as a sum of trigonometric functions greatly simplifies the study of heat transfer.

sublevels.name: Integral Transforms and Operational Calculus
sublevels.description: In mathematics, an integral transform maps an equation from its original domain into another domain where it might be manipulated and solved much more easily than in the original domain. The solution is then mapped back to the original domain using the inverse of the integral transform.Operational calculus, also known as operational analysis, is a technique by which problems in analysis, in particular differential equations, are transformed into algebraic problems, usually the problem of solving a polynomial equation.

sublevels.name: Real Functions
sublevels.description: A function of a real variable is a function whose domain is the real numbers ℝ, or a subset of ℝ that contains an interval of positive length. Most real functions that are considered and studied are differentiable in some interval. The most widely considered such functions are the real functions, which are the real-valued functions of a real variable, that is, the functions of a real variable whose codomain is the set of real numbers

sublevels.name: Special Functions
sublevels.description: Special functions are particular mathematical functions which have more or less established names and notations due to their importance in mathematical analysis, functional analysis, physics, or other applications

sublevels.name: Functions of a Complex Variable
sublevels.description: Complex analysis, traditionally known as the theory of functions of a complex variable, is the branch of mathematical analysis that investigates functions of complex numbers. As a differentiable function of a complex variable is equal to the sum of its Taylor series, complex analysis is particularly concerned with analytic functions of a complex variable (that is, holomorphic functions).

sublevels.name: Integral Equations
sublevels.description: Integral equations are equations in which an unknown function appears under an integral sign.

sublevels.name: Stochastic Integral Equations
sublevels.description: Stochastic Integral Equations are a type of mathematical equations that involve both stochastic processes and integrals. These equations combine the concepts of stochastic calculus and integral equations, providing a framework to study dynamic systems subject to random influences.

sublevels.name: Abstract Harmonic Analysis
sublevels.description: Harmonic analysis is a branch of mathematics concerned with the representation of functions or signals as the superposition of basic waves, and the study of and generalization of the notions of Fourier series and Fourier transforms.

sublevels.name: Several Complex Variables and Analytic Spaces
sublevels.description: "Several Complex Variables" and "Analytic Spaces" are branches of mathematics that deal with complex analysis in higher dimensions. These terms and concepts form the foundation of the study of several complex variables and analytic spaces, exploring complex analysis in higher dimensions and its applications to areas such as complex geometry, potential theory, and singular spaces.

sublevels.name: Difference and Functional Equations
sublevels.description: In mathematics, a functional equation is any equation in which the unknown represents a function. Often, the equation relates the value of a function (or functions) at some point with its values at other points. The term functional equation usually refers to equations that cannot be simply reduced to algebraic equations.A difference equation is an equation that recursively defines a sequence or multidimensional array of values, once one or more initial terms are given: each further term of the sequence or array is defined as a function of the preceding terms.

sublevels.name: Approximations and Expansions
sublevels.description: In mathematics, approximation theory is concerned with how functions can best be approximated with simpler functions, and with quantitatively characterizing the errors introduced thereby.

sublevels.name: Operator Theory
sublevels.description: Operator theory is the study of linear operators on function spaces, beginning with differential operators and integral operators. The operators may be presented abstractly by their characteristics, such as bounded linear operators or closed operators, and consideration may be given to nonlinear operators. The study, which depends heavily on the topology of function spaces, is a branch of functional analysis.

sublevels.name: Differential Equations
sublevels.description: A differential equation is an equality constraining a mathematical function in relation to its derivatives over one or multiple variables. Such equations may constitute the mathematical model for a natural system, whose behaviour may be predicted upon their analytical resolution or through computer simulation.

sublevels.name: Ordinary Differential Equations
sublevels.description: In mathematics, an ordinary differential equation (ODE) is a differential equation containing one or more functions of one independent variable and its derivatives. The term ordinary is used in contrast with the term partial differential equation which may be with respect to more than one independent variable.

sublevels.name: Partial Differential Equations
sublevels.description: In mathematics, a partial differential equation (PDE) is a differential equation that contains beforehand unknown multivariable functions and their partial derivatives. PDEs are used to formulate problems involving functions of several variables, and are either solved by hand, or used to create a computer model.

sublevels.name: Optimization
sublevels.description: Optimization is a mathematical and computational process of finding the best solution to a problem within a given set of constraints. It involves maximizing or minimizing an objective function, subject to certain constraints, in order to achieve the optimal outcome

sublevels.name: Discrete Optimization
sublevels.description: An optimization problem with discrete variables is known as a discrete optimization, in which an object such as an integer, permutation or graph must be found from a countable set.

sublevels.name: Operations Research, Management Science
sublevels.description: Operations Research is a discipline that deals with the development and application of analytical methods to improve decision-making. The term management science is occasionally used as a synonym.

sublevels.name: Calculus of Variations and Optimization
sublevels.description: The "Calculus of Variations" and "Optimization" are branches of mathematics that deal with finding optimal solutions to problems involving functions. These terms and concepts form the foundation of the calculus of variations and optimization, which involve finding optimal solutions, characterizing critical points, and determining the best strategies for functionals and problems with constraints. These fields have applications in physics, engineering, economics, control systems, machine learning, and many other areas.

sublevels.name: Continuous Optimization
sublevels.description: As opposed to discrete optimization, the variables used in the objective function are required to be continuous variables—that is, to be chosen from a set of real values between which there are no gaps (values from intervals of the real line). Because of this continuity assumption, continuous optimization allows the use of calculus techniques.

sublevels.name: Topology
sublevels.description: In mathematics, topology is concerned with the properties of space that are preserved under continuous deformations, such as stretching, twisting, crumpling and bending, but not tearing or gluing.

sublevels.name: Manifolds and Cell Complexes
sublevels.description: including Differential Topology

sublevels.name: Algebraic Topology
sublevels.description: Algebraic topology is a branch of mathematics that uses tools from abstract algebra to study topological spaces. The basic goal is to find algebraic invariants that classify topological spaces up to homeomorphism, though usually most classify up to homotopy equivalence

sublevels.name: Geometry
sublevels.description: Geometry  is a branch of mathematics concerned with questions of shape, size, relative position of figures, and the properties of space

sublevels.name: Projective Geometry
sublevels.description: Projective geometry is the study of geometric properties that are invariant with respect to projective transformations. Compared to elementary geometry, projective geometry has a different setting, projective space, and a selective set of basic geometric concepts. The basic intuitions are that projective space has more points than Euclidean space, for a given dimension, and that geometric transformations are permitted that transform the extra points (called "points at infinity") to Euclidean points, and vice versa

sublevels.name: Convex and Discrete Geometry
sublevels.description: Convex geometry is the branch of geometry studying convex sets, mainly in Euclidean space. Most questions in discrete geometry involve finite or discrete sets of basic geometric objects, such as points, lines, planes, circles, spheres, polygons, and so forth

sublevels.name: Combinatorial Geometry
sublevels.description: Combinatorial geometry studies combinatorial properties and constructive methods of discrete geometric objects and focuses on the combinatorial properties of these objects, such as how they intersect one another, or how they may be arranged to cover a larger object

sublevels.name: Patterning
sublevels.description: A pattern is a regularity in the world, man-made design, or abstract ideas. As such, the elements of a pattern repeat in a predictable manner. A geometric pattern is a kind of pattern formed of geometric shapes and typically repeated like a wallpaper design. Geometric patterning is the study of such patterns (mathematics Springer).Patterning describes the processes by which the plan for later development of a plant is laid down. It involves the early establishment of 'prepatterns' of 'morphogens' which form a complex signalling network, which in turn determines further differentiation (Nature)

sublevels.name: Computational Geometry
sublevels.description: Computational geometry is a branch of computer science devoted to the study of algorithms which can be stated in terms of geometry

sublevels.name: Tiling
sublevels.description: Tiling in geometry is the study of the covering of a plane using one or more geometric shapes, called tiles, with no overlaps and no gaps. In mathematics, tessellations/tilings can be generalized to higher dimensions and a variety of geometries. Mathematicians use many technical terms when discussing tilings

sublevels.name: Hyperbolic Geometry
sublevels.description: Hyperbolic geometry (also called Bolyai–Lobachevskian geometry or Lobachevskian geometry) is a non-Euclidean geometry. Hyperbolic plane geometry is also the geometry of saddle surface or pseudospherical surfaces, surfaces with a constant negative Gaussian curvature

sublevels.name: Polytopes
sublevels.description: In elementary geometry, a polytope is a geometric object with "flat" sides. It is a generalization in any number of dimensions of the three-dimensional polyhedron. Polytopes may exist in any general number of dimensions n as an n-dimensional polytope or n-polytope

sublevels.name: Differential Geometry
sublevels.description: Differential geometry is a mathematical discipline that uses the techniques of differential calculus, integral calculus, linear algebra and multilinear algebra to study problems in geometry. The theory of plane and space curves and surfaces in the three-dimensional Euclidean space formed the basis for development of differential geometry during the 18th century and the 19th century

sublevels.name: Shape Analysis
sublevels.description: The study that deals with the mathematical representation, comparison, and manipulation of shapes or geometrical objects. It involves developing techniques to extract meaningful information from shapes, quantify their similarities or differences, and perform various operations based on shape-related attributes.

sublevels.name: Mathematical Logic and Foundations
sublevels.description: Mathematical logic explores the applications of formal logic to mathematics. It bears close connections to metamathematics, the foundations of mathematics, and theoretical computer science. The unifying themes in mathematical logic include the study of the expressive power of formal systems and the deductive power of formal proof systems. Foundations of Mathematics is the study of the philosophical and logical and/or algorithmic basis of mathematics, or, in a broader sense, the mathematical investigation of what underlies the philosophical theories concerning the nature of mathematics. Foundations of mathematics can be conceived as the study of the basic mathematical concepts (set, function, geometrical figure, number, etc.) and how they form hierarchies of more complex structures and concepts, especially the fundamentally important structures that form the language of mathematics (formulas, theories and their models giving a meaning to formulas, definitions, proofs, algorithms, etc.) also called metamathematical concepts, with an eye to the philosophical aspects and the unity of mathematics.

sublevels.name: Model Theory
sublevels.description: Model theory is the study of the relationship between formal theories and their models.

sublevels.name: Computability and Recursion Theory
sublevels.description: Computability theory, also known as recursion theory, is a branch of mathematical logic, of computer science, and of the theory of computation that originated in the 1930s with the study of computable functions and Turing degrees.

sublevels.name: Set Theory
sublevels.description: Set theory is a branch of mathematics. It studies sets, which are collections of objects. Only those sets are objects of set theory, which are of relevance for mathematics as a whole.

sublevels.name: Algebraic Logic
sublevels.description: In mathematical logic, algebraic logic is the reasoning obtained by manipulating equations with free variables

sublevels.name: Proof Theory and Constructive Mathematics
sublevels.description: a method of proof that demonstrates the existence of a mathematical object by creating or providing a method for creating the object.

sublevels.name: Linear Logic
sublevels.description: Linear logic is a substructural logic proposed by Jean-Yves Girard as a refinement of classical and intuitionistic logic, joining the dualities of the former with many of the constructive properties of the latter.

sublevels.name: General Logic
sublevels.description: critical examination of how we acquire “scientific” knowledge, and of that knowledge itself, principles, general laws, and theories.

sublevels.name: Substructural Logics
sublevels.description: In logic, a substructural logic is a logic lacking one of the usual structural rules (e.g. of classical and intuitionistic logic), such as weakening, contraction, exchange or associativity. Two of the more significant substructural logics are relevance logic and linear logic.

sublevels.name: Algebra
sublevels.description: one of the broad parts of mathematics, in its most general form, algebra is the study of mathematical symbols and the rules for manipulating these symbols. It includes everything from elementary equation solving to the study of abstractions such as groups, rings, and fields

sublevels.name: Order, Lattices, Ordered Algebraic Structures
sublevels.description: A lattice is an abstract structure studied in the mathematical subdisciplines of order theory and abstract algebra. It consists of a partially ordered set in which every two elements have a unique supremum (also called a least upper bound or join) and a unique infimum (also called a greatest lower bound or meet). Lattices can also be characterized as algebraic structures satisfying certain axiomatic identities

sublevels.name: Commutative Rings and Algebras
sublevels.description: Commutative algebra is the branch of algebra that studies commutative rings, their ideals, and modules over such rings. It is the main technical tool in the local study of schemes

sublevels.name: Linear Algebra
sublevels.description: Linear algebra concerns linear equations, linear maps and matrices.

sublevels.name: Matrix Theory
sublevels.description: In mathematics, a matrix (plural: matrices) is a rectangular array of numbers, symbols, or expressions, arranged in rows and columns

sublevels.name: Multilinear Algebra
sublevels.description: In mathematics, multilinear algebra extends the methods of linear algebra, it builds on the concepts of p-vectors and multivectors with Grassmann algebra

sublevels.name: Field Theory and Polynomials
sublevels.description: In mathematics, a field is a set on which addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division are defined, and behave as the corresponding operations on rational and real numbers do. A field is thus a fundamental algebraic structure. A polynomial is an expression that is the sum of a finite number of non-zero terms, each term consisting of the product of a constant and a finite number of variables raised to whole number powers

sublevels.name: Category Theory
sublevels.description: Category theory formalizes mathematical structure and its concepts in terms of a labeled directed graph called a category, whose nodes are called objects, and whose labelled directed edges are called arrows (or morphisms).

sublevels.name: General Algebraic Systems
sublevels.description: General Algebraic Systems form a remodelling of the algebra from a structural viewpoint. Groups, rings and fields are instances of an algebraic system.

sublevels.name: Non-associative Rings and Algebras
sublevels.description: A non-associative algebra (or distributive algebra) is an algebra over a field where the binary multiplication operation is not assumed to be associative

sublevels.name: Associative Rings and Algebras
sublevels.description: an associative algebra is an algebraic structure with compatible operations of addition, multiplication (assumed to be associative), and a scalar multiplication by elements in some field. The addition and multiplication operations together give A the structure of a ring

sublevels.name: Topological Groups and Lie Groups
sublevels.description: A topological group is a mathematical object with both an algebraic structure and a topological structure. Thus, one may perform algebraic operations, because of the group structure, and one may talk about continuous functions, because of the topology. A Lie group is a group that is also a differentiable manifold, with the property that the group operations are compatible with the smooth structure.

sublevels.name: Group Theory and Generalizations
sublevels.description: In mathematics and abstract algebra, group theory studies the algebraic structures known as groups. The concept of a group is central to abstract algebra: other well-known algebraic structures, such as rings, fields, and vector spaces, can all be seen as groups endowed with additional operations and axioms

sublevels.name: Algebraic Geometry
sublevels.description: is a branch of mathematics, classically studying zeros of multivariate polynomials. Modern algebraic geometry is based on the use of abstract algebraic techniques, mainly from commutative algebra, for solving geometrical problems about these sets of zeros

sublevels.name: K-Theory
sublevels.description: In mathematics, K-theory is the study of a ring generated by vector bundles over a topological space or scheme

sublevels.name: Homological Algebra
sublevels.description: Homological algebra is the branch of mathematics that studies homology in a general algebraic setting. It is the study of homological functors and the intricate algebraic structures that they entail

sublevels.name: Discrete Mathematics
sublevels.description: Discrete mathematics is the study of mathematical structures that are fundamentally discrete rather than continuous. In contrast to real numbers that have the property of varying "smoothly", the objects studied in discrete mathematics – such as integers, graphs, and statements in logic – do not vary smoothly in this way, but have distinct, separated values.

sublevels.name: Applications of Discrete Mathematics
sublevels.description: mathematical structures and objects that are fundamentally discrete, rather than continuous. common applications of discrete mathematics: It is used in the analysis and design of algorithms, data structures, cryptography, network protocols, and database systems,  modeling and solving optimization problems, such as resource allocation, scheduling, logistics, and network flow problems.

sublevels.name: Number Theory
sublevels.description: study of properties, relationships, and patterns related to integers and their properties. It involves exploring the properties of numbers, their divisibility, prime factorization, congruences, Diophantine equations, arithmetic functions, and other fundamental concepts in number theory.

sublevels.name: Computational Number Theory
sublevels.description: Computational number theory is the branch of number theory concerned with finding and implementing efficient computer algorithms for solving various problems in number theory.

sublevels.name: Algorithmic Complexity
sublevels.description: Algorithmic complexity is concerned about how fast or slow particular algorithm performs. We define complexity as a numerical function T(n) - time versus the input size n. We want to define time taken by an algorithm without depending on the implementation details.

sublevels.name: Complexity
sublevels.description: Complexity is the property of a system whose behaviour as a whole emerges as distinct from the simple sum of its individual behaviours. The understanding of complex systems is therefore beyond the linear algebra of classic reductionism and requires either statistical methods or computer simulations

sublevels.name: History of Mathematical Sciences
sublevels.description: The history of mathematical sciences dates back thousands of years and spans various cultures and civilizations. The development of mathematics has been influenced by the practical needs of societies, philosophical inquiries, and intellectual curiosity.

sublevels.name: General Mathematics
sublevels.description: General mathematics is the non‑specialized introduction to mathematical ideas, combining topics such as arithmetic, basic algebra, geometry, and practical problem‑solving. It is typically designed for learners who need a wide foundation, emphasizing everyday applications and logical thinking.

sublevels.name: Mathematics in Popular Science
sublevels.description: Mathematics plays a crucial role in popular science, providing a foundation for understanding and explaining various scientific concepts and phenomena. By utilizing mathematics, popular science endeavors to convey scientific concepts, theories, and discoveries to a wider audience, making science more accessible, engaging, and understandable for non-experts.

sublevels.name: Statistics
sublevels.description: Statistics is the application of mathematical concepts to understanding and analysing large collections of data. A central tenet of statistics is to describe the variations in a data set or population using probability distributions. This analysis aids understanding of what underlies these variations and enables predictions of future changes.

sublevels.name: Statistics and Computing
sublevels.description: Statistics and Computing are two interconnected fields that work together to analyze and interpret data using computational techniques and statistical methodologies.

sublevels.name: Markov Process
sublevels.description: Markov processes are stochastic processes, traditionally in discrete or continuous time, that have the Markov property, which means the next value of the Markov process depends on the current value, but it is conditionally independent of the previous values of the stochastic process. In other words, the behavior of the process in the future is stochastically independent of its behavior in the past, given the current state of the process. Markov processes form an important class of stochastic processes and have applications in many areas

sublevels.name: Brownian Motion
sublevels.description: Brownian motion or pedesis (from Ancient Greek: πήδησις) is the random motion of particles suspended in a fluid (a liquid or a gas) resulting from their collision with the fast-moving molecules in the fluid. This pattern of motion typically alternates random fluctuations in a particle's position inside a fluid sub-domain with a relocation to another sub-domain. Each relocation is followed by more fluctuations within the new closed volume. This motion is named after the botanist Robert Brown, who was the most eminent microscopist of his time

sublevels.name: Diffusion Process
sublevels.description: Diffusion is the passive movement of molecules or particles from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration

sublevels.name: Statistical Software
sublevels.description: Statistical software are specialized computer programs for analysis in statistics and econometrics.

sublevels.name: Statistical Learning
sublevels.description: Statistical learning is the study of how to understand, model, and predict patterns in data using both probabilistic theory and algorithmic methods. It covers a spectrum from classical statistical models to modern machine‑learning techniques that learn structure from data.

sublevels.name: Machine Learning
sublevels.description: Machine learning (ML) is the scientific study of algorithms and statistical models that computer systems use to progressively improve their performance on a specific task. Machine learning algorithms build a mathematical model of sample data, known as "training data", in order to make predictions or decisions without being explicitly programmed to perform the task. The study of mathematical optimization delivers methods, theory and application domains to the field of machine learning. In its application across business problems, machine learning is also referred to as predictive analytics

sublevels.name: Data Analysis and Big Data
sublevels.description: Data Analysis and Big Data are related fields that involve the exploration, interpretation, and extraction of insights from large and complex datasets.

sublevels.name: Big Data
sublevels.description: Big Data is a field of business and management research and practice that focuses on the collection, storage, processing, analysis, and interpretation of large and complex data sets generated by organizations, individuals, and machines. It involves the use of advanced technologies, statistical methods, and computational techniques to extract insights and value from these data sets. Some of the major topics in Big Data include: Data management: This includes the storage, retrieval, and processing of large data sets using various technologies such as Hadoop, NoSQL, and cloud computing. Data analytics: This involves the use of statistical methods and machine learning algorithms to analyze and extract insights from large data sets. Data visualization: This includes the creation of graphical representations of data to help users understand and interpret complex data sets. Data privacy and security: This topic deals with the protection of sensitive data from unauthorized access, use, and disclosure. Business intelligence: This involves the use of Big Data to support business decision-making by providing insights into customer behavior, market trends, and other relevant information. Data governance: This includes the development and implementation of policies, procedures, and standards for the management and use of data within organizations. Social media analytics: This involves the analysis of social media data to understand user behavior, preferences, and opinions. Internet of Things (IoT): This topic deals with the collection and analysis of data generated by connected devices and sensors. Predictive modeling: This involves the use of data to create models that can predict future events or behaviors. Data ethics: This topic deals with the ethical and moral considerations surrounding the collection, use, and analysis of data.

sublevels.name: Data Analytics
sublevels.description: Data analytics is the science of analyzing raw data to make conclusions about that information. Many of the techniques and processes of data analytics have been automated into mechanical processes and algorithms that work over raw data for human consumption.

sublevels.name: Applied Statistics
sublevels.description: Applied statistics is the use of statistical techniques to solve real-world data analysis problems. It is the root of data analysis, and the practice of applied statistics involves analyzing data to help define and determine organizational needs.

sublevels.name: Statistics in Engineering, Physics, Computer Science, Chemistry and Earth Sciences
sublevels.description: Statistics in Engineering, Physics, Computer Science, Chemistry, and Earth Sciences involves the application of statistical techniques to analyze data and solve problems in these scientific and technical fields.

sublevels.name: Statistical Physics
sublevels.description: Statistical physics is a branch of physics that uses probability theory and statistics to solve physical problems that usually involve systems composed of a large number of units. Its main purpose is to study the properties of a system from the statistical behaviour of its components.

sublevels.name: Statistical Mechanics
sublevels.description: A mathematical framework that applies probability theory and statistics to large assemblies of microscopic entities in order to derive macroscopic properties (temperature, pressure, entropy, magnetization) from microscopic laws of motion.

sublevels.name: Statistics in Business, Management, Economics, Finance, Insurance
sublevels.description: Statistics in Business, Management, Economics, Finance, Insurance involves the application of statistical methods to analyze data and inform decision-making in these fields, including risk assessment, market analysis, and performance evaluation.

sublevels.name: Financial Engineering
sublevels.description: Financial engineering is a multidisciplinary field that applies mathematical and quantitative methods to design, develop, and analyze financial products, instruments, and strategies. In research and practice, financial engineering involves a range of activities and tasks, including:  Design and development of financial products: The design and development of financial products such as derivatives, options, and futures contracts, which can be used to manage financial risk or to achieve specific investment objectives.  Risk management: The identification, assessment, and management of financial risks associated with various financial products and strategies, including credit risk, market risk, and operational risk.  Quantitative analysis: The use of mathematical and statistical models to analyze financial data and to develop strategies for managing financial risk.  Optimization of financial strategies: The development and optimization of financial strategies such as portfolio management, asset allocation, and hedging strategies, to achieve specific financial objectives such as maximizing returns or minimizing risk.  Pricing and valuation: The development of pricing and valuation models for financial products, to ensure that they are priced accurately and fairly.  Overall, the goal of financial engineering is to create innovative financial products and strategies that meet the needs of investors and financial institutions, while managing financial risk and achieving specific financial objectives. In practice, financial engineering is used by a range of financial institutions and organizations, including banks, hedge funds, insurance companies, and pension funds.

sublevels.name: Statistics in Social Sciences, Humanities, Law, Education, Behavorial Sciences, Public Policy
sublevels.description: Statistics is a branch of mathematics that involves the collection, analysis, interpretation, presentation, and organization of data. In the context of social sciences, humanities, law, education, behavioral sciences, and public policy, statistics plays a crucial role in providing a quantitative framework for studying and understanding various phenomena. It involves the application of statistical methods and techniques to examine patterns, relationships, and trends within data, ultimately facilitating evidence-based decision making and drawing valid conclusions.

sublevels.name: Statistical Theory and Methods
sublevels.description: Statistical Theory and Methods involve the study and application of mathematical principles and techniques for collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and making inferences from data. It encompasses the development and exploration of statistical models, estimation methods, hypothesis testing, and data analysis techniques.

sublevels.name: Scaling Laws
sublevels.description: Scaling laws describe the functional relationship between two physical quantities that scale with each other over a significant interval. An example of this is power law behaviour, where one quantity varies as a power of the other.

sublevels.name: Linear Models and Regression
sublevels.description: A linear regression model describes the relationship between a dependent variable, y, and one or more independent variables, X. Linear regression is one of the techniques statisticians use to estimate the parameters of a linear model.

sublevels.name: Mathematical Statistics
sublevels.description: Mathematical statistics is the application of probability theory, a branch of mathematics, to statistics, as opposed to techniques for collecting statistical data. Specific mathematical techniques which are used for this include mathematical analysis, linear algebra, stochastic analysis, differential equations, and measure theory

sublevels.name: Non-parametric Inference
sublevels.description: statistical techniques that use data to infer unknown quantities of interest while making as few assumptions as possible

sublevels.name: Parametric Inference
sublevels.description: Parametric statistics assumes that sample data comes from a population that can be adequately modeled by a probability distribution that has a fixed set of parameters.

sublevels.name: Design of Experiments
sublevels.description: Design of experiments (DOE) is defined as a branch of applied statistics that deals with planning, conducting, analyzing, and interpreting controlled tests to evaluate the factors that control the value of a parameter or group of parameters. It allows for multiple input factors to be manipulated, determining their effect on a desired output.

sublevels.name: Bayesian Inference
sublevels.description: Bayesian inference is a statistical method of inductive reasoning based on the reassessment of competing hypotheses in the presence of new evidence. Conceptually similar to the scientific method itself, formal Bayesian techniques are increasingly used in Artificial Intelligence and Brain models for decision-making under uncertainty.

sublevels.name: Stochastic Modelling
sublevels.description: "Stochastic" means being or having a random variable. Stochastic modelling is the development of mathematical models for non-deterministic physical systems, which can adopt many possible behaviours starting from any given initial condition. Monte-Carlo simulations, for example, consist of exploring the various possible states of a complex probabilistic system. A stochastic model is a tool for estimating probability distributions of potential outcomes by allowing for random variation in one or more inputs over time. through random sampling of initial conditions and repeated computer simulations.

sublevels.name: System Robustness
sublevels.description: Robustness is the property of a system whose behaviour is relatively insensitive to perturbations either in its environment or in its components. There is often a trade-off between robustness and adaptability.

sublevels.name: Methodology of Data Collection and Processing
sublevels.description: systematic approach and techniques used to gather and analyze data in order to derive meaningful insights and draw conclusions

sublevels.name: Survey Methodology
sublevels.description: Survey methodology is "the study of survey methods". As a field of applied statistics concentrating on human-research surveys, survey methodology studies the sampling of individual units from a population and associated techniques of survey data collection, such as questionnaire construction and methods for improving the number and accuracy of responses to surveys.

sublevels.name: History of Statistics
sublevels.description: The history of statistics can be traced back to ancient civilizations, where rudimentary methods of data collection and analysis were used. Over time, the field of statistics has evolved, incorporating new techniques and theories to better understand and interpret data.

sublevels.name: Computer Science
sublevels.description: Computer science is the study and development of the protocols required for automated processing and manipulation of data. This includes, for example, creating algorithms for efficiently searching large volumes of information or encrypting data so that it can be stored and transmitted securely..Computational science is a discipline concerned with the design, implementation and use of mathematical models to analyse and solve scientific problems. Typically, the term refers to the use of computers to perform simulations or numerical analysis of a scientific system or process..Information theory and computation is the study and development of protocols and algorithms for solving problems and analysing information. This discipline usually breaks information down into individual bits, and then determines the optimum logical operation required to efficiently process this data in any required way..Information technology is the design and implementation of computer networks for data processing and communication. This includes designing the hardware for processing information and connecting separate components, and developing software that can efficiently and faultlessly analyse and distribute this data.

sublevels.name: Artificial Intelligence
sublevels.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is intelligence demonstrated by machines, unlike the natural intelligence displayed by humans and animals, which involves consciousness and emotionality. The distinction between the former and the latter categories is often revealed by the acronym chosen. 'Strong' AI is usually labeled as AGI (Artificial General Intelligence) while attempts to emulate 'natural' intelligence have been called ABI (Artificial Biological Intelligence). Leading AI textbooks define the field as the study of "intelligent agents": any device that perceives its environment and takes actions that maximize its chance of successfully achieving its goals. Colloquially, the term "artificial intelligence" is often used to describe machines (or computers) that mimic "cognitive" functions that humans associate with the human mind, such as "learning" and "problem-solving".

sublevels.name: Symbolic AI
sublevels.description: In symbolic AI (Artificial Intelligence) knowledge is represented in the form of human-readable symbols and rules, and reasoning and problem-solving is performed by manipulating these using logical inference and search. Applications include knowledge-based systems such as expert systems, planning systems, ontologies, and intelligent tutoring systems (ITS).

sublevels.name: Knowledge Based Systems
sublevels.description: Knowledge-based systems are computer programs that use a centralized repository of data known as a knowledge base to provide a method for problem-solving. Knowledge-based systems are a form of artificial intelligence (AI) designed to capture the knowledge of human experts to support decision-making.

sublevels.name: Natural Language Processing (NLP)
sublevels.description: Natural language processing is an interdisciplinary subfield of linguistics, computer science, and artificial intelligence concerned with the interactions between computers and human language, in particular how to program computers to process and analyze large amounts of natural language data.

sublevels.name: Logic in AI
sublevels.description: In AI, logic is used as a formal language and a tool for representing and reasoning about knowledge, making inferences, and solving problems.

sublevels.name: Intelligence Augmentation
sublevels.description: Intelligence augmentation is the support of human thinking, analysis, and action using collaborative technological means. Intelligence augmentation treats humans as the decision-makers and supports them by predicting patterns, and creating knowledge bases and tools for activities such as image processing, natural language, and knowledge discovery. Examples of intelligence augmentation tools include virtual assistants, such as Siri, Alexa, and Google Home. Synonyms include augmented intelligence, intelligence amplification, assistive intelligence, cognitive augmentation, and machine-augmented intelligence.

sublevels.name: Intelligence Infrastructure
sublevels.description: A web of computation, data and physical entities exists that makes human environments more supportive, interesting and safe. Such infrastructure is beginning to make its appearance in domains such as transportation, medicine, commerce and finance, with vast implications for individual humans and societies.

sublevels.name: Multiagent Systems
sublevels.description: Multiagent systems are self-organized systems with interacting, autonomous agents that cooperate on a common objective. Applications include artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and modeling and negotiation in economics and social science.

sublevels.name: Data Structures and Information Theory
sublevels.description: Data Structures and Information Theory are two fundamental concepts in computer science and information theory that deal with the representation, organization, and manipulation of data and information. Data structures refer to the way data is organized and stored in a computer's memory or storage to facilitate efficient access, modification, and retrieval of information. while Information theory is a branch of applied mathematics and computer science that studies the quantification, storage, transmission, and processing of information.

sublevels.name: Data Storage Representation
sublevels.description: Data storage representation refers to the way data is organized, stored, and represented in computer systems. It involves the conversion of data from its original form to a format suitable for storage and retrieval in computer memory or secondary storage devices.

sublevels.name: Data Science
sublevels.description: Data science is an interdisciplinary academic field that uses statistics, scientific computing, scientific methods, processes, algorithms and systems to extract or extrapolate knowledge and insights from noisy, structured, and unstructured data.

sublevels.name: Data Structures
sublevels.description: Data structures are fundamental concepts in computer science that define the organization and storage of data in a computer's memory or storage devices. They provide a systematic way to manage and manipulate data efficiently, enabling various algorithms and operations to be performed effectively. Different data structures are designed to suit specific types of data and the operations that need to be performed on them.

sublevels.name: Theory of Computation
sublevels.description: Theory of computation (TOC) is concerned with how problems can be solved using algorithms and how efficiently they can be solved.

sublevels.name: Computer Science Logic and Foundations of Programming
sublevels.description: Includes verification, temporal logic, automated reasoning, logic programming, description logics, finite model theory, programming logic, model checking, formal methods, type systems, algebraic semantics, categorical semantics, program analysis, program verification, abstraction

sublevels.name: Computational Complexity
sublevels.description: Computational comlexity studies the minimal resources required to solve a computational problem, It includes complexity classes, proof complexity, interactive proof systems. It deals with the study of the resources required to solve computational problems. Computational complexity provides valuable insights into the inherent difficulty of problems and helps classify them based on their tractability or intractability.

sublevels.name: Models of Computation
sublevels.description: Includes computability, concurrency, hybrid models, abstract machines, quantum computing, abstract machines. Models of Computation refer to abstract, mathematical, or theoretical frameworks used to study the capabilities and limitations of computation. These models help computer scientists and mathematicians analyze and understand different computational problems and algorithms in a formal and rigorous manner.

sublevels.name: Quantum Computing
sublevels.description: Quantum computing is computing using quantum-mechanical phenomena, such as superposition and entanglement. The relative device is called quantum computer.

sublevels.name: Theory and Algorithms for Application Domains
sublevels.description: Includes machine learning theory (models of learning, reinforcement learning, Markov decision processes, inductive inference, online learning theory, support vector machines), algorithmic game theory and mechanism design (market equilibria, network games, auctions), theory of random search heuristics

sublevels.name: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
sublevels.description: Includes graph algorithms, approximation algorithms, mathematical optimization, online algorithms, parameterized complexity, streaming algorithms, parallel algorithms, distributed algorithms, design and analysis of data structures (data compression, pattern matching, sorting, searching), algorithm design techniques

sublevels.name: Information Model
sublevels.description: An information model in software engineering is a representation of concepts and the relationships, constraints, rules, and operations to specify data semantics for a chosen domain of discourse.

sublevels.name: Formal Languages and Automata Theory
sublevels.description: Includes grammars and context-free languages, tree languages, formalisms. It studies the formal languages and abstract machines used to describe and recognize patterns and structures in strings and sequences. It  have practical applications in various areas of computer science, including compiler design, programming language design, parsing, pattern matching, and natural language processing

sublevels.name: Theoretical Computer Science
sublevels.description: Theoretical computer science or TCS studies the fundamental mathematical principles of computation, the .mathematical principles, theories, and techniques. It encompasses the mathematical foundations of algorithms, data structures, computational models, and computational complexity.

sublevels.name: Coding and Information Theory
sublevels.description: Coding and information theory are closely related fields within computer science and mathematics. Coding theory deals with the design and analysis of error-correcting codes, which are used to transmit data reliably over noisy channels. Information theory, on the other hand, focuses on quantifying and measuring information and communication.

sublevels.name: Information Theory
sublevels.description: Information theory is the scientific study of the quantification, storage, and communication of information.  Applications range from data telecommunications to evolution, brain science and cosmology. This scientific field is at the intersection of probability theory, statistics, computer science, statistical mechanics, information engineering, and electrical engineering.

sublevels.name: Symbolic and Algebraic Manipulation
sublevels.description: The study and development of algorithms and software for manipulating mathematical expressions and other mathematical objects.

sublevels.name: Computer and Information Systems Applications
sublevels.description: Computer and Information Systems Applications refer to the practical use and application of computer technology and information systems in various domains. It involves utilizing computer software, hardware, networks, and databases to solve problems, streamline processes, and support decision-making.

sublevels.name: Computer Application in Administrative Data Processing
sublevels.description: The use of computer systems and software to manage and process administrative data in various organizational settings. These applications streamline and automate administrative tasks, improving efficiency, accuracy, and data accessibility.

sublevels.name: Smart Infrastructure
sublevels.description: Intelligent interconnection of energy systems, buildings and industry platforms incl. the control thereof by collecting and processing the generated data

sublevels.name: Computer-Aided Engineering (CAD, CAE) and Design
sublevels.description: Computer-aided engineering (CAE) is the broad usage of computer software to aid in engineering analysis tasks.  By simulating performance, product designs are improved and optimized. CAE primarily uses computer-aided design (CAD) next to computer-aided manufacturing (CAM). It is often summarized in the collective abbreviation "CAx".

sublevels.name: Computer Modelling
sublevels.description: Computer modelling consists of writing a computer program version of a mathematical model for a physical or biological system. Computer simulations that are run according to such programs can produce knowledge out of reach of mathematical analysis or natural experimentation. Computational models are mathematical models used to numerically study the behaviour of complex systems by means of a computer simulation. A computational model can be used to make predictions of the system's behaviour under different conditions, often for cases in which intuitive analytical solutions are not available.

sublevels.name: Building Information Modeling
sublevels.description: Meaning information modeling for buildings; used in architecture / civil engineering for maintaining and communicating information systems and data related to buildings

sublevels.name: Complex Systems
sublevels.description: Complex systems is a scientific field that studies the common properties of systems considered complex in nature, society, and science. It is also called complex systems theory, complexity science, study of complex systems and/or sciences of complexity. The key problems of such systems are difficulties with their formal modeling and simulation. From such perspective, in different research contexts complex systems are defined on the base of their different attributes. As an interdisciplinary domain, complex systems draws contributions from many different fields, such as the study of self-organization from physics, that of spontaneous order from the social sciences, chaos from mathematics, adaptation from biology, and many others

sublevels.name: Computational Social Science, Social Networks
sublevels.description: Computational social science refers to the academic sub-disciplines concerned with computational approaches used to model, simulate, and analyze social phenomena. It focuses on investigating social and behavioral relationships and interactions through social simulation, modeling, network analysis, and media analysis.Social Networks aim to analyze the structure of whole social entities as well as a variety of theories explaining the patterns observed in these structures. The study of these structures uses social network analysis to identify local and global patterns, locate influential entities, and examine network dynamics.

sublevels.name: Biophysical Economics
sublevels.description: Biophysical economics is the study of the ways and means by which human societies procure and use energy and other biological and physical resources to produce, distribute, consume and exchange goods and services, while generating various types of waste and environmental impacts.

sublevels.name: Data-driven Science, Modeling and Theory Building
sublevels.description: Data-driven Science is an interdisciplinary field that uses scientific methods, processes, algorithms and systems to extract knowledge and insights from data in various forms. It employs several techniques and theories drawn from many fields within the context of mathematics, statistics, information science, and computer science.

sublevels.name: Complex Networks
sublevels.description: Complex networks are networks that feature patterns of connection between their elements that are neither purely regular nor purely random. Most real-world networks, such as transportation, social or gene-regulatory networks, are complex.

sublevels.name: Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos Theory
sublevels.description: Nonlinear Dynamics and its applications aims to solve different problems coming from many fields as chemistry, medicine, biology and engineering. It is the branch of physics that studies systems governed by equations more complex than the linear, aX+b form. Nonlinear systems, such as the weather or neurons, often appear chaotic, unpredictable or counterintuitive, and yet their behaviour is not random.Chaos theory focuses on the behavior of dynamical systems that are highly sensitive to initial conditions. It is an interdisciplinary theory stating that within the apparent randomness of chaotic complex systems, there are underlying patterns, constant feedback loops, repetition, self-similarity, fractals, self-organization, and reliance on programming at the initial point known as sensitive dependence on initial conditions.

sublevels.name: User Interfaces and Human Computer Interaction
sublevels.description: Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) is an interdisciplinary domain that involves the development and deployment of technologies centered on users, the field emphasizes user experience and accessibility. Related topics include user research; interface design; human factors such as emotion; and human control mechanisms using speech, haptics, or gesture.

sublevels.name: Bioinformatics
sublevels.description: Bioinformatics involves using approaches from computer science and statistics to analyze biological data. Tools include pattern recognition, visualization, machine learning, and data mining, Application domains include genomics, proteomics, drug discovery, and systems biology.

sublevels.name: Product Design and Prototyping
sublevels.description: Product Design is the process of conceptualizing, designing, testing, and refining products,  digital services, or experiences to solve user problems

sublevels.name: Database Management System
sublevels.description: A Database Management System (DBMS) is software that enables the creation, organization, management, and retrieval of data from a database.

sublevels.name: Information Storage and Retrieval
sublevels.description: The process of storing and accessing information in a structured and efficient manner. It involves the organization, indexing, and retrieval of data and documents to meet users' information needs

sublevels.name: Database Management
sublevels.description: A database is one or more sets of data, for example numbers, characters and images, bundled together with software that enables data to be added, removed or retrieved. Databases can be used to store research data, for example in protein databases and genetic databases, and they organise data into standard formats so that information can readily be obtained.

sublevels.name: Programming Language
sublevels.description: A programming language is a set of symbols whose strings are governed by rules apt to communicate instructions to a particular machine. Such strings may be concatenated into longer code and implement abstract algorithms in the form of programs specific to actual computing devices.

sublevels.name: Java
sublevels.description: Java is a high-level, class-based, object-oriented programming language that is designed to have as few implementation dependencies as possible. It is a general-purpose programming language intended to let programmers write once, run anywhere (WORA) meaning that compiled Java code can run on all platforms that support Java without the need to recompile.

sublevels.name: Python
sublevels.description: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language. Its design philosophy emphasizes code readability with the use of significant indentation via the off-side rule

sublevels.name: C++
sublevels.description: C++ is a widely used programming language that is known for its versatility and efficiency. It is an extension of the C programming language and supports both procedural and object-oriented programming paradigms.

sublevels.name: Lisp
sublevels.description: Lisp programming language, Common Lisp. Lisp, short for "List Processing," is a high-level programming language known for its unique and distinctive syntax and its powerful support for symbolic data manipulation and functional programming.  It was designed to be a practical tool for artificial intelligence (AI) research, and its strong emphasis on symbolic computation and recursion made it an ideal choice for processing symbolic data and solving complex problems.

sublevels.name: Perl
sublevels.description: Perl is a high-level, general-purpose programming language known for its versatility, flexibility, and powerful text-processing capabilities. Perl stands for "Practical Extraction and Reporting Language," but it is also known as the "Pathologically Eclectic Rubbish Lister" due to its various and eclectic features.

sublevels.name: JavaScript
sublevels.description: JavaScript is a high-level, interpreted programming language primarily used to create interactive and dynamic content on websites. It runs in web browsers and enables features like animations, form validation, and real-time updates.

sublevels.name: Rust
sublevels.description: Rust is a general purpose programming language designed for safety, speed, and concurrency. It eliminates typical programming errors like memory leaks and data races.

sublevels.name: Computer Hardware
sublevels.description: Hardware refers to the external and internal devices and equipment that enables to perform major functions such as input, output, storage, communication, processing, and more.

sublevels.name: Logic Design
sublevels.description: Logic design is a field of engineering that focuses on the design and implementation of digital circuits and systems using logic gates and Boolean algebra. It involves the process of transforming a set of specifications or requirements into a logical representation that can be implemented using digital components and technologies.

sublevels.name: Control Structures and Microprogramming
sublevels.description: Control structures are programming constructs that enable the execution of different sections of code based on certain conditions or criteria. They determine the flow and order of program execution and allow for decision-making and repetition. While Microprogramming is a low-level design technique used in computer architecture to implement complex instructions and control the behavior of a processor. It involves breaking down complex instructions into a sequence of microinstructions that can be executed by the processor's control unit.

sublevels.name: Robotics
sublevels.description: Design of robots and the respective control systems, engineering, programming and teaching-in. study, design, and development of robots and autonomous systems. Robots are machines or mechanical devices that can perform tasks autonomously or semi-autonomously, either by following pre-programmed instructions or through artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms.

sublevels.name: Brain-machine Interface
sublevels.description: A brain–machine interface (BMI) is a device that translates neuronal information into commands capable of controlling external software or hardware such as a computer or robotic arm. BMIs are often used as assisted living devices for individuals with motor or sensory impairments.

sublevels.name: Computer Memory Structure
sublevels.description: The memory structure of a computer refers to those hardware elements that store the data elements and the related information during program execution

sublevels.name: Processor Architectures
sublevels.description: A processor architecture attempts to compromise between the needs of programs hosted on the architecture and the performance attainable in implementing the architecture.

sublevels.name: Maker
sublevels.description: Arduino, Raspberry Pi, sensor networks, sensors, xbee, 3D printing

sublevels.name: Register-Transfer-Level Implementation
sublevels.description: a design abstraction which models a synchronous digital circuit in terms of the flow of digital signals (data) between hardware registers, and the logical operations performed on those signals.

sublevels.name: Input/Output and Data Communications
sublevels.description: Input and output, as the process names suggest is the data communication going in and out of a machine. More specifically, input is the name given to digital signals and data incoming, while output is the outgoing data. The process of input/output involves input/output operations.

sublevels.name: Hardware Performance and Reliability
sublevels.description: Hardware performance and reliability are two critical aspects of computing systems that directly impact their functionality, efficiency, and user experience

sublevels.name: Arithmetic and Logic Structures
sublevels.description: An arithmetic and logic structures is the part of a central processing unit that carries out arithmetic and logic operations on the operands in computer instruction words. In some processors, the ALU is divided into two units: an arithmetic unit (AU) and a logic unit (LU)

sublevels.name: Data and Information Security
sublevels.description: Data security is the process of safeguarding digital information throughout its entire life cycle to protect it from corruption, theft, or unauthorized access

sublevels.name: Cryptology
sublevels.description: Cryptology is the study and implementation of techniques for secure communication in the presence of adversaries. Cryptography involves constructing and analyzing protocols that prevent third parties or the public from reading private messages. Cryptanalysis involves trying to break these cryptographic approaches. Related topics include: Encryption; Decryption; Key Management; Public-Key Cryptography, Public-Key Encryption, Asymmetric Cryptography, Digital Signatures; Elliptic Curve Cryptography; Symmetric Cryptography, Hash Functions, Block Ciphers, Stream Ciphers, Message Authentication Codes (MACs); Cryptanalysis, Cryptanalytic Attacks; Confidentiality; Data Integrity; Authentication; Smartcards; Passwords; Privacy; Quantum Cryptography; Ciphers; Random-Oracle Model; Cryptocurrencies; Cryptographic Hardware; Side-Channel Attacks; Untraceability; Pseudo-Random Sequences; Multiparty Computation; Lattice Algorithms, Lattice-Based Cryptography; Provable Security; Post-Quantum Cryptography; and supporting foundational and mathematical concepts from Computational Complexity Theory, Computational Number Theory, Information Theory.

sublevels.name: Computer Crime
sublevels.description: Computer Crime is a generic designation of a type of crime that involves or exploits weaknesses in computers and computer networks. This may also mean that a computer or electronic device may have been used in the commission of a crime. Common targets include: electronic devices such as a computer or cellphones; ATMs; individuals; companies; national security, finance, or healthcare systems; or critical infrastructure such as power grids, dams, or electricity-generating plant. Related topics include: audit trails; botnets; computer forensics; computer fraud; computer immunology; computer virus; computer virology; critical infrastructure protection (CIP); critical national infrastructure (CNI); cryptoworm; cryptovirology; cyber attacks or cyberattacks; cyber crime or cybercrime; cyber stalking or cyberstalking; cyber terrorism or cyberterrorism; cyber war or cyberwar; data recovery; data remanence; data theft; digital blackmail; digital evidence; digital extortion; digital forensics; firewall; hacking; honeypot; intrusion-detection systems (IDS); kleptography; malware; network intrusion; ransomware; security logs; spam; steganography; Trojans.

sublevels.name: IT Risk Management
sublevels.description: Risk management is the identification, evaluation, and prioritization of risks (defined in ISO 31000 as the effect of uncertainty on objectives) followed by coordinated and economical application of resources to minimize, monitor, and control the probability or impact of unfortunate events or to maximize the realization of opportunities

sublevels.name: IT Security Awareness
sublevels.description: Knowledge and attitude regarding IT security aspects. The level of understanding and consciousness that individuals and organizations have about potential security threats and best practices to protect information technology (IT) systems and data. It involves educating users and employees about the importance of cybersecurity and fostering a security-conscious culture within an organization. IT Security Awareness aims to promote responsible behaviors and actions to mitigate risks and prevent security breaches.

sublevels.name: Security Services
sublevels.description: A processing or communication service that enhances the security of the data processing systems and the information transfers of an organization. These services are intended to counter security attacks, and they make use of one or more security mechanisms to provide the service.

sublevels.name: Mobile and Network Security
sublevels.description: set of technologies that protects the usability and integrity of a company's infrastructure by preventing the entry or proliferation within a network of a wide variety of potential threats.

sublevels.name: Principles and Models of Security
sublevels.description: The basic tenets of information security are confidentiality, integrity and availability. Every element of the information security program must be designed to implement one or more of these principles. Together they are called the CIA Triad.

sublevels.name: Blockchain
sublevels.description: A blockchain is a dynamic list of records called blocks that are linked over time. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, a timestamp and transaction data. By design, a blockchain is resistant to modification of its data. The concept of a blockchain was invented to serve as the public transaction ledger of the cryptocurrency Bitcoin. For use as a distributed ledger, a blockchain is typically managed by a peer-to-peer network collectively adhering to a protocol for inter-node communication and for validating new blocks. Although blockchain records are not unalterable, blockchains may be considered secure by design and exemplify a distributed computing system with high Byzantine fault tolerance. Associated concepts include: Ethereum, smart contracts, Byzantine protocol, decentralized control.

sublevels.name: Digital Privacy
sublevels.description: Digital privacy is the ability to protect information about an individual or group. Related concepts include human, societal, and economic aspects of information security privacy; privacy-preserving data mining and information retrieval, and related usability tradeoffs; differential privacy and other cryptography and information security approaches to defining and quantifying privacy loss; legal frameworks such as GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) in the context of information privacy and data protection; privacy-preserving authentication; privacy-enhancing technologies and privacy by design; and end-to-end security and encryption.

sublevels.name: Computer Imaging, Vision, Pattern Recognition and Graphics
sublevels.description: Computer imaging, vision, pattern recognition, and graphics are interdisciplinary fields that involve the analysis, understanding, and manipulation of visual data using computers. Computer imaging refers to the acquisition, processing, and manipulation of digital images using computers,  Computer vision aims to enable computers to gain a high-level understanding of visual information from images or video sequences, Pattern recognition involves the automated identification and classification of patterns or regularities in data, Computer graphics deals with the creation, manipulation, and rendering of visual content using computers.

sublevels.name: Biometrics
sublevels.description: It involves the use of biological traits to verify and recognize individuals, providing a more secure and reliable method compared to traditional identification methods such as passwords or ID cards.

sublevels.name: Computer Vision
sublevels.description: Computer vision is a field of artificial intelligence (AI) that enables computers and systems to derive meaningful information from digital images, videos and other visual inputs — and take actions or make recommendations based on that information.

sublevels.name: Automated Pattern Recognition
sublevels.description: process of developing algorithms and systems that can automatically identify patterns or regularities in data without human intervention. It involves the use of machine learning, artificial intelligence, and statistical techniques to train computer systems to recognize and classify patterns in various types of data, including images, sounds, texts, and numerical data
